Member Cruson asked if they have the capability to resubmit their application as a new
application. Chairman Seaworth said that there are different options. The first option is for
the applicant to withdraw their application, and they would be able to resubmit a new
application at a future date. The second option is for the Planning Board to decide that
they do not want to grant the extension to the applicant and to deny the application without
prejudice, which would allow the applicant to resubmit the application. Lastly, if the
Planning Board decides that they do not want to grant the extension to the applicant and to
deny the application for cause, the applicant cannot reapply unless there is a substantial
change to the site plan.
Selectmen's Rep Frederickson noted that the applicant seems to want to negotiate.
Chairman Seaworth spoke about the time limit and stated that the current law states that if
there is no vote at this meeting, and there is no extension given, then the application would
go to the Selectboard, and they must automatically approve the application.
Planner Cronin added that the Selectboard cannot place any conditions on the approval.
Chairman Seaworth stated that this is a new process and there is not a lot of familiarity or
history on how the process works. Previously, the Board would continue applications as
necessary to get the information needed. This has tightened up a lot more under the
current law.
Member Cravotta asked what would happen if an extension was granted and the new
deadline was not met. Chairman Seaworth clarified that they requested two things. The
first was an extension of the 65-day time limit through the May meeting. They also asked
to continue the hearing so they would have time to prepare. If the Planning Board is back
the next month, all the same options would be on the table if an extension was granted. If
there was no resolution at the next meeting, the Planning Board would be given the same
options that they have at the current meeting. There is no limit if there is agreement
between parties.
MOTION: Member Cruson made a motion to deny Major Site Plan Application #25-101
without prejudice. Member Hanson seconded the motion.
Chairman Seaworth stated that this denial would be based on the Planning Board not
having enough information to evaluate the proposal.
Member Cruson listed her concerns from multiple departments. These included comments
presented at the Technical Review Committee (TRC) and previous meetings. Specifically,
the following comments had not been addressed: Water Department comments requesting
the water main be extended with individual shutoffs, the Police Department's request for
numbering on each unit, the Planning's request for parking spaces conforming to
traditional lengths of 19 feet and a truck turnaround for dumpster services. Also, the Fire
Department stated that the road was not adequate for service and stated that they would
not approve the plan as submitted. They also requested a change in the location of
hydrant and an extension of the driveway. The Town Engineer had comments regarding
drainage and several other items. There may also be issues with inadequate snow
storage. Member Cruson noted that she never has that many concerns about a project.
Chairman Seaworth asked the Board if they had any further comments on the motion.

application. The 65-day review timeclock will expire on May 1st. The hearing on April 22nd
is the last meeting before the expiration. The Applicant was notified of the upcoming
deadline and was asked that they submit an extension request if they wished to continue
with the review process for further opportunity to discuss the application and work through
any outstanding issues.
On the afternoon of April 22nd,
", a request was received from the applicant to continue the
application to the May 27th meeting and to extend the review deadline that the Planning
Board has to that date as well. Planner Cronin suggested that before the Board explored
staff comments and the merits of the plan, the request to extend the review period and
extend the public hearing to May 27t should be reviewed.
Chairman Seaworth noted that in State Law, this is done by agreement with both parties.
Based on the applicant's conversation with Planner Cronin, they have requested an
extension to the next meeting date. The Planning Board must agree to this.
Selectmen's Rep Frederickson asked if the applicant is seeking to have more time to
comply with the outstanding items. Planner Cronin stated that the applicant communicated
to her that they have not completed the revised plans to address the outstanding
comments. Selectmen's Rep Frederickson asked if they still wanted to proceed. Planner
Cronin stated that the applicant would like to continue the process, which is why they have
requested an additional month.
Member Cruson asked Chairman Seaworth if any progress had been made on the many
issues that were relayed to them to be corrected. Chairman Seaworth stated that this could
not be answered since they have not turned anything in. They also have not detailed what
they are working on.
Planner Cronin stated that there has not been any new information since the submittal on
March 18th. Member Cruson asked for confirmation that they had not addressed comments
regarding water issues, the Police Department numbering request, the Town Engineer's
comments, or the Fire Department comments. Planner Cronin stated that they had
addressed some comments but had not addressed most of the comments from town
departments.

Page 2 of 30

Member Cruson asked if they have the capability to resubmit their application as a new
application. Chairman Seaworth said that there are different options. The first option is for
the applicant to withdraw their application, and they would be able to resubmit a new
application at a future date. The second option is for the Planning Board to decide that
they do not want to grant the extension to the applicant and to deny the application without
prejudice, which would allow the applicant to resubmit the application. Lastly, if the
Planning Board decides that they do not want to grant the extension to the applicant and to
deny the application for cause, the applicant cannot reapply unless there is a substantial
change to the site plan.
Selectmen's Rep Frederickson noted that the applicant seems to want to negotiate.
Chairman Seaworth spoke about the time limit and stated that the current law states that if
there is no vote at this meeting, and there is no extension given, then the application would
go to the Selectboard, and they must automatically approve the application.
Planner Cronin added that the Selectboard cannot place any conditions on the approval.
Chairman Seaworth stated that this is a new process and there is not a lot of familiarity or
history on how the process works. Previously, the Board would continue applications as
necessary to get the information needed. This has tightened up a lot more under the
current law.
Member Cravotta asked what would happen if an extension was granted and the new
deadline was not met. Chairman Seaworth clarified that they requested two things. The
first was an extension of the 65-day time limit through the May meeting. They also asked
to continue the hearing so they would have time to prepare. If the Planning Board is back
the next month, all the same options would be on the table if an extension was granted. If
there was no resolution at the next meeting, the Planning Board would be given the same
options that they have at the current meeting. There is no limit if there is agreement
between parties.
MOTION: Member Cruson made a motion to deny Major Site Plan Application #25-101
without prejudice. Member Hanson seconded the motion.
Chairman Seaworth stated that this denial would be based on the Planning Board not
having enough information to evaluate the proposal.
Member Cruson listed her concerns from multiple departments. These included comments
presented at the Technical Review Committee (TRC) and previous meetings. Specifically,
the following comments had not been addressed: Water Department comments requesting
the water main be extended with individual shutoffs, the Police Department's request for
numbering on each unit, the Planning's request for parking spaces conforming to
traditional lengths of 19 feet and a truck turnaround for dumpster services. Also, the Fire
Department stated that the road was not adequate for service and stated that they would
not approve the plan as submitted. They also requested a change in the location of
hydrant and an extension of the driveway. The Town Engineer had comments regarding
drainage and several other items. There may also be issues with inadequate snow
storage. Member Cruson noted that she never has that many concerns about a project.
Chairman Seaworth asked the Board if they had any further comments on the motion.

Vice Chairman Edmonds thinks that the Board should defer this discussion until there is a

property tor themselves. Since the cattle farm is the primary use at this time, it is subject to

plan exemptions for agricultural use. The plan requires a Wetlands Special Use Permit
(SUP) for impacts to the buffer. The proposed location of the pole barn extends into the
50-foot wetland buffer.

to allow commercial agricultural use on the property.

March 10, 2025, meeting and expressed concerns about manure management best
practices and felt that the pole barn could be relocated outside of the buffer area.

Proposed streets, Test pits, Topography, Proposed easements, Location of existing water,
sewer, and drainpipes, Construction plans, Roadway profiles, Roadway cross-sections,

construction.

January 28, 2025 meeting. The Board voted that this was a Development of Regional
Impact (DRI) at that time, therefore the application process was paused while impacted
parties were notified. He asked Planner Cronin to give an update on the status of the

CNHRP had two recommendations. They believe that there may be regional impacts
because of the proximity to share aquifers or surface waters and shared facilities. They
recommended that the Planning Board ensure that the proposal complies with their MS4
Ordinance. Also, they added that the Planning Board should ensure that stormwater runoff
is minimized and treated properly prior to running into the Suncook River. They stated that
requiring that the proposal comply with the recommendations of Pembroke's Town
Engineer would be the best way to ensure that the proposal complies with MS4
requirements.
Planner Cronin stated that there were no further comments.
Chairman Seaworth asked if the Board had any comments prior to the opening of the
public hearing. There were none.
At 6:35 pm, Chairman Seaworth opened the Public Hearing on the application. He
reminded the public that if the application was not completed at this meeting, the public
hearing would also be continued and would not be renoticed. Members of the public must
state their name and street for the record. All comments need to be addressed to the
Chair.
John Noonan, Fieldstone Land Consultants, was present to discuss the application on
behalf of MJ Properties NH, LLC. The application is for a 12-unit multifamily residential
dwelling. There is an existing conditions plan. The property is undeveloped. They have
done test pits. They have designed the site, which is similar to what was submitted for their
Special Exception, which was approved by Zoning. There are 6 units with driveways and 6
with 2 parking spaces available for a total of 24 parking spaces.
Based on the aquifer overlay, there is a Special Use Permit. The residential use will
connect to municipal sewer on Buck Street. This will be upgraded and extended. As part of
the MS4 requirement, they will be extending municipal water. This will be used for fire flow
and domestic water.
Based on feedback from the Technical Review Committee (TRC), they will be widening
Wilkins Avenue to the minimum of 20 feet paved based on town requirements. Sewer and
water connection comments will be addressed per TRC comments and state requirements
as well. There were also comments on this from Underwood Engineers. The two
comments from CHRPC fall under the comments from TRC regarding MS4 requirements
for sewer and stormwater.
Mr. Noonan then reviewed the plans with the Board. There is a central driveway coming off
Wilkins Avenue. The mailboxes will be moved according to TRC comments. Also, there is
an extension of where the dumpster is so there is a turnaround, which will also allow for
clearance for fire trucks.
There was also a grading and drainage plan. He explained the plan, which will allow
drainage to a detention basin, which will ultimately tie to a pipe that will be extended to the
infrastructure on Buck Street. This has been redesigned with the new paving plan for
Wilkins Avenue.

They have submitted a utilities sheet which shows the extension of water and sewer down
Wilkins Avenue. There were TRC comments on hydrants and shut offs for each unit. Each
unit will also have a 911 address, as well as be notated alphabetically (A through F). There
is also underground electric from the overhead line.
There was a lighting plan submitted. There are three pole mounted lights on the parking
light side where there are no driveways. On the side with driveways, the lighting will be
affixed to the building. There will also be lighting for the dumpster that will be pole
mounted.
There was a landscaping plan submitted. Mr. Noonan described these plans to the Board.
There were also erosion control, pavement, concrete, construction, stormwater and sewer
notes submitted. Pembroke and the Department of Environmental Services (DES) will
review the sewer notes.
Mr. Noonan stated that there are revisions needed to address TRC comments, and they
will be reaching out to the Town Engineer to review the utilities. They will also be
addressing Underwood comments. He was also open to addressing comments from the
audience.
Chairman Seaworth asked the applicant to remind him of what the Underwood comments
referred to. Planner Cronin stated that Underwood Engineers is a consultant for the Sewer
Commission. Mr. Noonan added that they have put up the escrow for this work to be done.
Chairman Seaworth opened the floor for questions from the Board. Vice Chairman
Edmonds inquired about the sewer and water connections that will be extended up Wilkins
Avenue. He assumed that this has been discussed thoroughly with the Sewer
Commission. Mr. Noonan stated that they have the comments from Underwood Engineers,
as well as comments from TRC that they will be addressing. They will be meeting with
Underwood Engineers about the quality of the sewer lines on Buck Street.
Vice Chairman Edmonds asked if the Commission has given any feedback on the
availability of capacity for the site. Mr. Noonan stated that he is aware that there have been
issues with capacity in the past, but he spoke about the increased capacity received by the
Town of Pembroke and stated that this has not been an issue that has been brought to his
attention. Sewer flow rates have been provided. Vice Chairman Edmonds mentioned that
there have been issues with developers not being able to secure the capacity needed for
development and that the Board had been told that this would be resolved. He wanted to
make sure that this has been discussed with the applicant. Mr. Noonan stated that this has
not been brought up as an issue with this project.
Planner Cronin stated that several years ago, capacity was an issue for this project. She
believed that capacity was resolved at the Zoning Board prior to coming to Planning.
Chairman Seaworth mentioned that he believed that the current capacity was enough to
cover all the projects in the pipeline.
Member Cruson remembers seeing the previous plans and the wetlands were in another
location. She asked who had reviewed the wetlands on the plan. Mr. Noonan stated that
Chris Guida, a wetlands scientist for his office, had reviewed the wetlands on the property.

affixed to the building. There will also be lighting for the dumpster that will be pole

There were minor plan revisions from the Technical Review Committee (TRC) meeting
such as dumpster location, outdoor lighting and changes to the parking striping. These
items were added to the plan and distributed to the Board.
There was an outstanding question on the number of bedrooms that will inform the sewer
proposal. The Department of Public Works (DPW) has requested a condition assessment
of the existing stormwater system to ensure that there are no issues in connection to the
town system in a way that is detrimental to the town and that there is no private stormwater
or sewer impacting the site systems. There have been some issues in the Village with not
knowing where pipes are, which has caused subsequent issues.
Chairman Seaworth asked if the changes in site plan had been reviewed by staff. Planner
Cronin stated that it was not distributed to any department. The Fire Department needs to
review the parking lot striping.
Chairman Seaworth asked if there were any outstanding items from TRC. Planner Cronin
stated that the only two outstanding items are the request for the bedroom count and the
request from DPW for the condition assessment for the stormwater system. There are no
further plan changes required.
At 6:37 pm, the Public Hearing was opened. Chairman Seaworth stated that if any
members of the public wished to speak, they must state their name and street address.
Also, any questions or comments must be addressed to the Chair. If for any reason the
application is not completed at this meeting and is continued to a future meeting, the public
hearing will be continued as well and will not be renoticed.
David Walch, Trustee for Athens Street Capital Realty Trust 24, was in attendance as the
property owner. Mr. Walch began by stating that the application seeks to turn the old bank
building into 12 apartment units. He stated that everything from the TRC was address on
the plan. He walked through plan updates regarding the dumpster location and exterior
lighting. There will be a parking space removed to accommodate the drive aisle
requirements per the Fire Departments request. There will be a minimum of 20 feet of
clearance.
The architectural plans will be finalized, and the number of bedrooms will be disclosed with
the building permits, and they will work with Water and Sewer. There will be between 22
and 27 bedrooms. There will be no studios at this point.
Chairman Seaworth clarified that the request for the amount of bedrooms was from Sewer
and not something that the Planning Board needed to review.
Vice Chairman Edmonds stated that he thinks it is a good plan overall. He mentioned that
the DPW Director is concerned about the condition and status of current drainage on the
site to be compatible with MS4 requirements. He asked if that was something that the
applicant was prepared to follow through with.
Mr. Walch stated that Fieldstone has been out to survey the current structures and found
no obstructions. He plans to work with the Sewer Department to see how in depth they
would like the review (i.e. video). He is hoping to get the as-built of the street sewer
connections. They can then go into the building and review the sewer lines. There are
C:\Users\LWilliams|AppData\Loca/\Microsoft|Windows\/NetCache|Content.Outlook\3FVT66LG\01-28-2025 Minutes
(Approved).docx
January 28, 2025 Planning Board Minutes
Page 2 of 17

limited sewer lines in the basement, but none that will be kept. They have been out of
service for the better part of two decades. He is hoping that the as-built of the current
building matches what the town has on record.
Chairman Seaworth clarified that although it is in the MS4 area, it is not subject to the
regulations because it does not propose a disturbance of natural vegetation. He felt that
this seems to be a very straightforward application of the regulations. Everything is already
existing. It is not a matter of creating new drainage or stormwater run-off.
Gerard Fleury, 21 Kimball Street, is an abutter. He would urge the Board to look favorably
on this project. The property has fallen into neglect. He thinks fixing it up will not only
provide additional residential housing, but there will also be someone onsite for upkeep.
He thinks this would be a good thing for the area.
A resident of Buck Street asked if anything would be done with the retaining wall that is
cracked on the property.
Mr. Walch stated that they would look at it, although it is very far away from the building.
He cannot make any promises. He will look at it and make sure there are no real structural
issues. He has not inspected it yet.
Desiree Caron, 66 Glass Street, asked if there was any proposed earth work or any
alterations to existing fence lines or curbs.
Chairman Seaworth stated that the short answer is no. Mr. Walch confirmed that there will
be no changes to fences, driveways or curbs.
Chairman Seaworth added that there is more than enough parking and this was discussed
at TRC. He asked Mr. Walch to explain how they are thinking of maintaining the parking lot
for the residents.
Mr. Walch stated that it would be great to develop the site, but at this point he is only
looking at the 12 units. He added that it would probably be in the best interest of the
community to fortify the retaining wall by adding townhouses there on the back side. He
stated again that this is not under serious contemplation. Fieldstone has not been asked to
do any preliminary work on this. There would certainly be enough land and parking.
Selectmen's Rep Frederickson was curious if the applicant would be willing to share
parking for things like snow emergencies since there is a surplus of parking spaces. He
stated that this would not impact the application in any way and was just an inquiry.
Mr. Walch stated that he is not opposed to it. He has not been policing it and has not
marketed or leased any spots. It does not bother him at all. He mentioned that he may be
interested in leasing parking spaces in the future.
There were no further questions from the Board.
Chairman Seaworth asked for a review of the conditions of approval.

Pembroke Planning Board
July 28, 2026
Meeting Minutes
(Approved on August 11, 2026)
Attendance
MEMBERS PRESENT: Brian Seaworth, Chairman; Bryan Christiansen, Selectmen's Rep;
Clint Hanson; Brent Edmonds; Robert Bourque, Vice Chair; Kathy Cruson
MEMBERS EXCUSED: Joshua Bursey
STAFF PRESENT: David Jodoin, Town Administrator
Chairman Seaworth called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
New Business
1. Major Site Plan Application #26-102, Tim Bradley, Cordwood Yard, LLC acting
as Applicant on behalf of Sheep Davis Realty, LLC, owner of Tax Map 561, Lot
11-1 located at 103 Sheep Davis Rd. in the Commercial/Light Industrial (C1)
Zone and the Aquifer Conservation (AC) District.
The Applicant proposes to construct a commercial wood processing yard with
associated access, parking, and site improvements.
• Special Use Permit Application SUP-AC #26-303
The Applicant requests a Special Use Permit in accordance with Article 143-68.E.,
Aquifer Conservation District, for construction over the aquifer.
Chairman Seaworth explained that this is a proposal to construct a cordwood processing
yard on a small, undeveloped lot on Route 106. It includes parking, storage shelter,
storage containers, storage areas, and stormwater infrastructure. There is no proposal to
connect to water or sewer. Being on Route 106 it will require a NHDOT driveway permit.
This application requires a special exception from the Zoning Board which the applicant
applied for and was granted by the Zoning Board on April 27th of this year and the Special
Use Permit is required because it's in the aquifer conservation district overlay.
The Chair noted that the plans had been revised on July 22nd to scale back the project for
the applicant's budget constraints and that review should focus on the revised plan set.
There are application waivers requested for items not proposed in the project, including
burglar and fire alarm information, hazardous material storage information and MSDS
sheets, multifamily housing, outdoor lighting, parks and open space, proposed streets,
roadway profiles, and roadway cross sections.
Vice Chair Bourque asked about storage of hazardous materials and MSDS, and that the
applicant assure that no chemicals will be used at any time onsite. Chairman Seaworth
explained that that can be discussed with the applicant during public hearing. At this point,
they are submitting the waiver request as their application does not propose it.
MOTION: Member Edmonds made a motion to grant the waiver requests for checklist
items:
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026\07-28-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
July 28, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 1 of 6

Part A. Items I, L, and Q; Part B. Items B.(7) and B.(11); and Part C. Items B. and C.
Member Hanson seconded the motion.
Member Cruson asked about the waiver from security lighting. Chairman Seaworth noted
that the waiver request is because they did not propose any. There was discussion about
this at TRC and we can discuss with the applicant. If we find it is needed, we can require
that as a condition, but it is not proposed on the plan as presented.
VOTE:
B. Seaworth - Y
K. Cruson - N
B. Christiansen - Y
B. Bourque - N
C. Hanson - Y
B. Edmonds - Y
The motion passed on a 4-2 vote.
Chairman Seaworth noted that the staff report indicates that the application meets all the
zoning requirements with the Zoning Board approval for special exception.
MOTION: Member Hanson made a motion to accept the application as complete.
Selectmen's Rep Christiansen seconded the motion.
VOTE:
B. Seaworth - Y
K. Cruson - Y
B. Christiansen - Y
B. Bourque - Y
C. Hanson - Y
B. Edmonds - Y
The motion passed on a 6-0 vote.
Chairman Seaworth opened the public hearing at 6:41 pm. He stated that if the application
was not completed at the meeting, the public hearing would also be continued and would
not be renoticed.
Ting Chang, TF Moran appeared with applicant Tim Bradley, Cordwood Yard, LLC. Ms.
Chang presented the revised project as a two-acre undeveloped site with shared driveway
access to an existing driveway, and one-way circulation. The development is pretty simple
with an open-air 42-foot by 40-foot shelter, kiln, tumbler, wood processing area, log
storage, equipment storage, a porta-potty, and three parking spaces. For stormwater
management, we propose a grass swale and infiltration pond. It will treat and provide
recharge to groundwater. It is designed for a 50-year storm and all water will stay inside
the basin. The applicant stated that no water or sewer connections were proposed, and
electricity would be extended only for the kiln.
Member Cruson asked for an explanation of the process for cordwood. Tim Bradley
explained that they take in raw material of hardwood logs. The process involves cutting,
splitting, and drying, and then going into the tumbler. There is no debarking; the tumbler
would remove loose bark and debris, and then it goes out for delivery. The end product
would be used as firewood.
Vice Chair Bourque asked if any logs come from out of state. Mr. Bradley said it was all
New Hampshire hardwood. Vice Chair Bourque's concern is the ash borer insect. Are
there any chemicals sprayed on the wood as a pesticide? Mr. Bradley said no, they don't
use any chemicals on the wood. Vice Chair Bourque asked what happens with the debris
in the tumbler. Mr. Bradley said the material hauled away. It would be bark and loose
topsoil. It is not stored onsite.
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026\07-28-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
July 28, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 2 of 6

Selectmen's Rep Christiansen asked if the conveyor belt is electric or diesel fueled. Mr.
Bradley said it was all diesel powered. The equipment would be fueled by a 75-gallon fuel
cell mounted on a truck.
Ms. Chang noted that Water Works requested they keep a moveable spill kit onsite. We
noted it on the plan. Staff will be trained on how to use it.
Member Edmonds asked they would be able to satisfy the comments from the Fire
Department. The applicant said yes, the plans were revised to modify the location and
height of the wood storage. We will need to provide a letter stating it meets the Fire Code.
Chair Seaworth brought up some discussion items from TRC. Conservation was
concerned about sanitary waste and the long term maintenance of the stormwater system.
The applicant said the only sanitary waste will be from a porta-potty serviced by a
company. The stormwater management plan includes an inspection schedule and
maintenance plan.
There was a discussion about whether there were restrictions on moving wood between
counties.
The applicant explained the difference in the building design from the original plan to the
revised plan.
There was a discussion about security measures at the site, which would be seasonal with
only two part-time employees. The property will be gated and posted No Trespassing. The
applicant agreed cameras were a good idea. Outdoor lighting is not necessary for the
hours of work onsite. There are gates, but the property is not fenced.
Chairman Seaworth said that KV Partners sent a memo with their review of the updated
plan. He has no further issues with the plan from an engineering standpoint. He suggested
reviewing the conditions of approval as follows:
1. Prior to signature, all waivers and the date granted shall be listed on the plan.
2. Prior to signature, the plans shall be revised to address all review comments and
any applicable concerns and issues from the Town Engineer.
3. Prior to signature, the Fire Department shall review the revised layout of the plan
and any applicable concerns and issues shall be addressed.
4. Prior to signature, all conditions of approval shall be listed on the plan.
5. Prior to issuance of a building permit, the applicant shall provide a letter prepared
by an engineer, stating that the project will be compliant with NFPA 1 Fire Code,
Chapter 31, per Fire Department request.
6. NHDOT Driveway Permit is required.
7. The original signatures of all property owners shall be provided on the final plan.
8. The Site Plan Review and Special Use Permit Notices of Decision are to be
recorded at the Merrimack County Registry of Deeds.
9. Building plans to be reviewed by the Building Inspector and Fire Chief.
10. The site plan will not be considered as receiving final approval until all conditions of
approval are met.
Chairman Seaworth asked about the shared driveway and existing truck traffic. The
applicant proposes 2-3 truck trips per day. They submitted for the revised NHDOT permit

Pembroke Planning Board
May 12, 2026
Meeting Minutes
(Approved September 15, 2026)
Attendance
MEMBERS PRESENT: Brian Seaworth, Chairman; Brent Edmonds, Vice Chairman;
Bryan Christiansen, Selectmen's Rep; Clint Hanson; Joshua Bursey; Kathy Cruson; Robert
Bourque
STAFF PRESENT: Carolyn Cronin, Town Planner
Chairman Seaworth called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Old Business
1. Election of Vice Chair
Chairman Seaworth noted that the Selectboard appointed Robert Bourque from an
alternate to a regular member.
MOTION: Member Edmonds made a motion to nominate Robert Bourque as vice chair of
the planning board. Member Hanson seconded the motion.
VOTE: B. Seaworth - Y B. Edmonds - Y B. Christiansen - Y
C. Hanson - Y
J. Bursey - Y
K. Cruson - Y
The motion passed on a 6-0 vote. Robert Bourque was nominated and elected as chair.
2. 65-Day Review Limit Policy/Planning Board Rules of Procedure
Planner Cronin recapped that at the last workshop the Board considered including the 65-
Day Continuance Policy into the Rules of Procedure. She said there was discussion about
the number of continuances the board would permit and different scenarios when that
might arise. She sent the question to the town attorney and their opinion was in the board
member packet. The attorney's letter stated that they did not recommend a policy where
the board could require re-noticing at its discretion. The attorney's concern was that an
applicant would have no way of knowing when they need to re-notice abutters, and that the
board should choose a re-notice period and apply it to all applicants equally.
Member Bursey recalled they originally chose three continuances because each
continuance is one month. He brought up that it could be any length of time. He suggested
90 days.
Chairman Seaworth said the concern was more about the circumstances than the length of
time. They want to re-notice when time passes and nothing has happened in that time. He
noted that the policy must be worded carefully, whether it is worded by number of days or
number of continuances.
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026|05-12-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
May 12, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 1 of 5

Planner Cronin reviewed the language of the state statute and found there was no
guidance for towns on how to deal with extension or waivers of the 65-day review period.
Member Cruson noted that the law does not specify whether it is the board or the applicant
that initiates the request for an extension.
Selectmen's Rep Christiansen pointed out the problem that the policy is trying to solve is
the notice to abutters, so it doesn't matter if the board bases it off of number of days or
number of continuances.
The board discussed basing the policy on number of days rather than number of
continuances. 100 days was suggested. They discusses whether the 100 days would be
counted from the application deadline or the acceptance of the application as complete.
They spoke about how developments of regional impact play into the process. The
emphasis kept returning to the purpose of the policy, which was to benefit the abutters.
Planner Cronin noted that she would be responsible for keeping track of the number of
days because she would need to get money from the applicant ahead of time to send the
notices. Member Edmonds asked what would work best for the planning department.
Planner Cronin needed to consider how the timing of the process would work. She pointed
out how she may not know if an applicant is continuing until that night, and then the notice
would not be sent until that meeting is already postponed. Chairman Seaworth said the
notice would be for the following month to tell them that the hearing would take place and
that there is no way to know what might happen at the next meeting. He said it would
notice them of the next meeting outside of the 100-day window.
Planner Cronin noted that she should have the attorney draw up a template letter because
the wording would be different than a typical abutter letter. Her concern is also that if the
policy is not enforceable, and an applicant refuses to pay for re-noticing, then should she
send the letters at the cost to the town?
Member Hanson felt strongly that the applicant should pay the fee if they are the cause of
the delay. Chairman Seaworth felt that most applicants would not want a delay, they would
want a decision. Vice Chairman Bourque suggested that an applicant should withdraw if
they are not ready to be heard. Selectmen's Rep Christiansen noted that they cannot solve
every scenario and that they would just have to cross those bridges when they got to them.
Selectmen's Rep Christiansen asked if it was reasonable to ask the attorney to put in a
120-day period and a template abutter notice together. He also suggested that the attorney
might have some language for a re-noticing policy that the board can review, because
other towns must struggle with the same issue.
Member Bursey suggested that the board move forward with what they have, not including
the re-noticing portion, and see how it plays out over the next six months or so. If it is a
problem, they can modify the Rules of Procedure appropriately. If there is no clean
solution, and they are struggling to solve problems that don't exist, they can update the
Rules of Procedure at any time.
Chairman Seaworth noted that the current law change complicates things. One problem is
when an applicant appears for a hearing, and not knowing if they expect a board vote that
night. Another problem is when the hearing stretches out so long, that the board wonders if
they owe the abutters another letter so they do not lose track of it.
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026|05-12-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
May 12, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 2 of 5

Vice Chair Bourque noted that the chair states at the beginning of each hearing that the
application will be continued to a future meeting, if not resolved, and no other notice will be
sent, and that has worked. Chairman Seaworth agreed and said they have always put it on
the abutter to follow the application, but they become confused when applications are
continued or hearings are not opened, because they do not know the process.
Chairman Seaworth noted that it is not in the board's rules that an applicant must submit a
request to continue in writing at least one week in advance. That is the first paragraph of
the policy the board is considering. The other paragraph is whether the board needs a
policy to re-notice abutters, which is a separate issue. The board can adopt one or both.
Selectmen's Rep Christiansen reiterated that the attorney likely already has language that
the board can use, but they did not ask her that question. He suggested adopting the first
paragraph and tabling the re-notice section until legal weighs in.
MOTION: Selectmen's Rep Christiansen made a motion to adopt the policy that the
applicant must submit a continuance request in writing as least one week prior to the
meeting. Vice Chair Bourque seconded the motion.
VOTE: B. Seaworth - Y B. Edmonds - Y B. Christiansen - Y
C. Hanson - Y
J. Bursey - Y
K. Cruson - Y
B. Bourque - Y
The motion passed on a 7-0 vote. The first paragraph of the 65-Day Review Limit Policy
was adopted as a board policy.
MOTION: Selectmen's Rep Christiansen made a motion to adopt the Rules of Procedure
as amended. Vice Chair Bourque seconded the motion.
VOTE: B. Seaworth - Y B. Edmonds - Y B. Christiansen - Y
C. Hanson - Y
J. Bursey - Y
• K. Cruson - Y
B. Bourque - Y
The motion passed on a 7-0 vote. The Rules of Procedure were amended to include the
first paragraph of the 65-Day Review Limit Policy as well as the minor corrections in the
red-lined version.
New Business
There was no new business.

Pembroke Planning Board
April 28, 2026
Meeting Minutes
(Approved on September 15, 2026)
Attendance
MEMBERS PRESENT: Brian Seaworth, Chairman; Bryan Christiansen, Selectmen's Rep;
Clint Hanson; Robert Bourque, Alternate; Kathy Cruson; Brent Edmonds
MEMBERS EXCUSED: Joshua Bursey
STAFF PRESENT: Carolyn Cronin, Town Planner
Chairman Seaworth called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
New Business
1. Major Site Plan Application #26-101, William Davidson, PE, Hoyle, Tanner, and
Associates, Inc. acting as Applicant on behalf of William Young Properties,
LLC, owner of Tax Map 256, Lot 26-2 located at 802 Ricker Ra. in the
Commercial/Light Industrial (C1) Zone and the Aquifer Conservation (AC),
Wetlands Protection (WP), Floodplain Development (FD), and Shoreland
Protection (SP) Overlay Districts.
The Applicant proposes to construct a 19,200 SF building with office and garage
space and associated parking, utilities, and stormwater improvements.
• Special Use Permit Application SUP-AC #26-301
The Applicant requests a Special Use Permit in accordance with Article 143-
68.E., Aquifer Conservation District, for new construction over the aquifer.
Planner Cronin explained the application is a major site plan and aquifer special use permit
for a garage and office building. The property is also located in the wetlands, floodplain,
and shoreland overlays, but there was no work in any of those districts. The Health Officer
had no concerns about the aquifer. Water Work issued a letter with comments on the
existing diesel fuel tank and best management practices.
A waiver from parking was requested. Checklist waivers were requested for hazardous
materials, multifamily housing, MSDS, proposed streets, and roadway profiles and cross-
sections.
A TRC meeting was held on April 14th. Building plans, traffic, and protection of natural
resources were discussed. The Conservation Commission reviewed the plan at their April
13th meeting. They had questions and concerns about impact to the river and the long term
maintenance of the stormwater system. The Town Engineer issued a letter stating he had
no engineering concerns, but noted that the dumpster is not enclosed.
Planner Cronin recommended that the checklist waivers for multifamily housing, proposed
streets, roadway profiles and cross-sections were appropriate because they were not
applicable to the plan. Storage of hazardous materials and MSDS may also be appropriate
as there is no proposal to store materials in regulated quantities. She recommended that
the parking waiver may be appropriate since the calculation is based on a similar use, as
determined by the code enforcement officer, and not an exact use of the property.

Alternate Bourque asked about hazardous materials and MSDS. He said they are fine for
the property owner, but how do they know it won't be a problem for the future tenant? If
those items are waived now, does that waive it for everything? Planner Cronin said there
was a conversation about that at TRC. The checklist waiver is just to say that the plan has
enough information to be determined as complete. Chairman Seaworth added that waiving
the checklist does not waive the requirements. They can discuss those requirements and
conditions of approval during the hearing. Chairman Seaworth spoke about change of use
and said that if a tenant was considered a change of use, then they would have to come
back to the planning board for review.
MOTION: Member Edmonds made a motion to grant the waiver requests for checklist
items:
Part A. Items I., L., and Q.; Part B. Item B.(11); and Part C. Items B. and C.
Member Hanson seconded the motion.
VOTE:
B. Seaworth - Y
K. Cruson - Y
B. Christiansen - Y
B. Bourque - Y
C. Hanson - Y
B. Edmonds - Y
The motion passed on a 6-0 vote.
MOTION: Alternate Bourque made a motion to accept the application as complete.
Member Edmonds seconded the motion.
VOTE:
B. Seaworth - Y
K. Cruson - Y
B. Christiansen - Y
B. Bourque - Y
C. Hanson - Y
B. Edmonds - Y
The motion passed on a 6-0 vote.
Chairman Seaworth opened the public hearing at 6:42 pm. He stated that if the application
was not completed at the meeting, the public hearing would also be continued and would
not be renoticed.
Josh Howard and Bill Davidson from Hoyle Tanner were present to represent the
applicant. Mr. Howard said 23,200 square feet of gross floor area are proposed for the
office and garage building. 8,000 sf is office space. The intent is to partition the building
down the middle into two separate offices and garages. He said it is currently used as a
contractor yard with piles of material. The owner is Young's Paving and they have their
trucks out there.
Mr. Howard noted there are three existing stormwater ponds on the property. The building
is sited over one of them. That pond would be filled and water would be diverted to the
other two ponds to infiltrate. He said they are modifying an existing outlet control structure
to help meet treatment requirements for an Alteration of Terrain permit, which they
submitted and are waiting for comments on.
Mr. Howard spoke to the parking waiver, which is required because the use does not
exactly line up with the table in the regulations. A new well and septic are proposed.
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026\04-28-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
April 28, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 2 of 11

Electric is already on site. The area is industrial on Ricker Road near Concord Sand and
Gravel.
Selectmen's Rep Christiansen asked about the design of the building. Mr. Howard
explained that each garage has four bay doors and the partition separates the two halves.
Alternate Bourque asked if there would be any maintenance done on vehicles or
equipment. Mr. Howard said that they expect simple maintenance like oil changes and tire
changes. Maintenance is not the primary use of the building.
Alternate Bourque asked about the outdoor diesel tank. Mr. Howard said there is an
existing diesel tank at the existing garage. Water Works was looking for secondary
containment on the tank. Alternate Bourque asked how large the tank was. The applicant
was not sure. Selectmen's Rep Christiansen pointed out that in Water Works' letter they
said secondary containment was not required, but was a best management practice.
Chairman Seaworth asked if the interior of the building would be designed to contain any
leaks or spills on the floor. Mr. Davidson said that any materials would require a safety
data sheet per the regulations, and it is hard to say what those materials might be since
there is no tenant, but they would provided that once a tenant is selected. Alternate
Bourque asked if there would be any floor drains in the building. Mr. Davidson said they
are not proposed.
Member Edmonds asked if there would be any truck washing or equipment clean up on
site. Mr. Davidson said there could be and it may be done already onsite. Member
Edmonds asked if it involved any solvents or kerosene. Mr. Davidson did not believe so.
Member Edmonds asked if there was a designated truck washing area. Mr. Davidson was
not aware of one and said the proposal would be similar to the existing use, where they
wash their trucks periodically, and pointed out that there is sediment bay designed to catch
anything.
Member Edmonds asked about the phasing and asked when phase 2 might break ground.
The applicant said it would be built all at once, but was designed in phases to be more
financially feasible. He added that the septic is phased because it would be two separate
tenants and that is how the state requires you to permit it.
Chairman Seaworth asked if the phased septic plan would have any additional review by
the planning board or if the state handles it. Planner Cronin explained that the board would
just have to require the state septic approval as a condition of approval.
Chairman Seaworth explained that as long as the tenant space is the same use or an
approved use, there would be no further review by the planning board, so the board needs
to deal with the unknowns as conditions of approval. He noted that staff makes the
determination of a change of use.
Planner Cronin noted that the use is determined as "manufacturing or industrial
establishment," which is pretty broad. If the tenant wanted to do something in a different
use category and/or wanted to expand the building, or if the parking were increased, the
site plan regulations determine what triggers a site plan review.

She included minor updates: grammatical corrections, updated administrative policies and
state statutes, and corrected inconsistencies. The major change was to add the 65-day
policy to Section 6.9, Continuance of Hearings.
Member Cruson asked if legal had any comments on the board's decision to include a

Members agreed with putting the policy in Section 6.9 of the Rules of Procedure, but still

Members agreed with the minor changes to the Rules of Procedure.
Chairman Seaworth suggested members review and see if they have any other issues

Pembroke Planning Board
March 24, 2026
Meeting Minutes
(Approved on September 15, 2026)
Attendance
MEMBERS PRESENT: Brian Seaworth, Chairman; Brent Edmonds, Vice Chairman;
Bryan Christiansen, Selectmen's Rep; Clint Hanson; Robert Bourque, Alternate; Kathy
Cruson; Joshua Bursey
MEMBERS EXCUSED: Angela Delaney
STAFF PRESENT: Carolyn Cronin, Town Planner
Chairman Seaworth called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Chairman Seaworth asked Alternate Bourque to vote for Member Delaney.
Old Business
1. Site Plan Regulations Updates
The board picked up where they left off from the last meeting reviewing proposed changes
to the Site Plan Regulations.
Planner Cronin explained that the Site Plan Fee Schedule is incorporated as a section of
the regulations. She wondered if this is better as an appendix to make updates easier. The
checklists are an appendix. The Select Board have authority to update the fee schedule
and then the Planning Board would need to update the site plan regulations with those
changes.
Chairman Seaworth pointed out that there would still have to be a public hearing to update
an appendix.
Selectmen's Rep Christiansen asked if the fees need to be adjusted. Planner Cronin said
the fees have not been updated since 2014; the only change since then is to the mailing
fee. She had looked at what other towns' applications fees are and they were all over the
place; there is no standard. She suggested that changes to the fees would need to be a
larger conversation.
Alternate Bourque suggested the application fees should be a percentage of the wage of
the employee who does the paperwork. Chairman Seaworth said that the fees have never
been set to break even or be revenue. He said it is part of the town's responsibility to
provide this service to applicants. He sees Alternate Bourque's point, but that's not how
other fees are calculated across towns. He added that would be up to the Select Board.
Planner Cronin agreed that the fee should not be arbitrary; there should be a process to
determine those numbers.
Chairman Seaworth said it doesn't hurt to move the fee schedule to the appendix. It fits
well with the forms that are in the appendix.
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026\03-24-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
March 24, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 1 of 8

Member Bursey asked about the process for adoption. He noted that the fee schedule said
it was adopted by the Board of Selectmen, but there is nothing noting that the Planning
Board adopted it. Did the Planning Board ever adopt these fees? Is there a process to
reflect that? Planner Cronin was unsure of what happened in 2014. She said the mailing
fees were adopted last year by the Select Board and the site plan regulations don't reflect
that, so there is a gap in that process. Member Bursey suggested that it would then require
adoption by the Planning Board.
Planner Cronin pointed out grammatical errors and editor's notes that were struck from the
regulations.
Chairman Seaworth spoke about the requirement for recording plans. He was not
comfortable with a proposed change that may make the applicant think that a requirement
was optional. Member Cruson asked about subdivision plans getting recorded. Planner
Cronin confirmed that subdivision plans must be recorded, but commercial site plans are
not recorded unless there is a condominium. Chairman Seaworth retracted his concern
after re-reading the verbiage.
Planner Cronin discussed the plan checklists for minor and major site plans. The site plan
application form includes the plan checklist. Those application forms have been updated in
recent years, but the checklists in the regulations were not adopted to reflect those
changes. She amended the checklists in the regulations to match the checklists in the
application forms, which is what the board currently reviews.
Chairman Seaworth wondered if there was an easy way to ensure that these checklists
would remain updated. Planner Cronin agreed that maybe another town has a better
process. Her imminent concern was that the checklists that the board currently uses are
not reflected in the regulations, and the regulations are what would be upheld in court (the
application form is just administrative). Chairman Seaworth wondered whether the
checklists needed to be included in the regulations at all. Planner Cronin strongly
recommended if not having the checklists themselves in the regulations, then having the
information from them elsewhere in the regulations. She said the application forms should
follow the regulations, not vice versa. She suggested maybe another town has a better
structure or format. She stressed the importance of consistency throughout the
regulations.
Planner Cronin updated the checklists to add hazardous materials, chemicals, and MSDS.
She struck contiguous buildable area because it was struck from the regulations. She
corrected a typo, updated the soil data, and added a "signature date" to the signature
block.
Member Cruson asked about the checklist item for impact to abutters. Planner Cronin
explained that the checklist item about abutter impacts is very limited in scope and only
relative to the construction plans. She clarified that it applied to impacts from the
construction process and not the long-term impacts of the development.

Pembroke Planning Board
February 24, 2026
Meeting Minutes
(Approved on August 11, 2026)
Attendance
MEMBERS PRESENT: Brian Seaworth, Chairman; Brent Edmonds, Vice Chairman; Rick
Frederickson, Selectmen's Rep; Clint Hanson; Robert Bourque, Alternate; Kathy Cruson
MEMBERS EXCUSED: Joshua Bursey; Angela Delaney
STAFF PRESENT: Carolyn Cronin, Town Planner
Chairman Seaworth called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Chairman Seaworth asked Alternate Bourque to vote for Member Bursey for this meeting.
Old Business
1. Site Plan Regulations Updates
It had been about 8 months since the Site Plan Regulations update was last reviewed.
Planner Cronin reported that the Board was to review red-line amendments to the
regulations which were to update out of date laws and policies and to codify the
regulations to the more recently updated plan checklists for consistency.
The Board left off on pages 203-14 and 203-15. From the last time, there were questions
on what a Certificate of Approval was, as referenced in the regulations. Planner Cronin
read the existing verbiage and noted that it does not follow current practice and
recommended that reference to a Certificate of Approval be struck. She explained that
other towns, including Concord, use that process, but there is no evidence Pembroke has
ever used it. Pembroke historically uses the notice of decision and staff just ensures that
those conditions are met. No additional document is issued when the conditions are met.
Planner Cronin suggested that the regulations reflect the actual practices and policies of
the town and the board.
Alternate Bourque asked if the signed Mylar would act as the same thing. Planner Cronin
confirmed and recommended that the signature block be amended to add a "Date Signed"
line in addition to the date of the conditional approval. The signature is the date of final
approval, and that should be recorded because the final approval is relative to vesting.
Selectmen's Rep Frederickson suggested that if it is not difficult, why not come up with a
certificate of approval form instead of two signatures or two dates on the final plan. He
pointed out that the regulations say that the certificate goes to multiple departments and
the applicant. He suggested those offices get the certificate. Planner Cronin pointed out
that those offices also get a set of plans.
Chairman Seaworth added that in a larger organization like Concord, where there are
many more people and departments, it may make sense that a form goes around to make
sure that everyone is OK signing off. Pembroke has one office, so it probably is not an
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026\02-24-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
February 24, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 1 of 5

issue that requires extra tracking. Adding the date of signature to the final plan may
remove the extra step of adding paperwork.
Selectmen's Rep Frederickson understood and was OK with whatever process closes the
loop.
Planner Cronin pointed out that the date of final signature does not matter to any other
town department (building, assessing), it only matters for legal issues for the planning
board. The issue is that the date of signature is not recorded, which should be resolved.
Alternate Bourque and Member Cruson asked about the signature block and what gets
recorded at the County. There was a discussion about the process of final approval, how it
is recorded, and what does it mean.
Planner Cronin would prefer to change "certificate of approval" to "endorsed plan". There
are two other references to certificate of approval in the regulations that would need to be
changed. She recommends legal counsel review this and advise.
Upon re-reading, it appeared that the certificate of approval is actually the notice of
decision. Chairman Seaworth suggested removing the certificate of approval language,
making minor tweaks to its other references, and clarifying the process of distributing the
plan copies. The Board agreed.
The next item to review was 203-23.A. There had been confusion about what it meant.
Upon re-reading, Planner Cronin suggested that it was a grammatical error that was
missing a period and a comma. Chairman Seaworth suggested another change to clarify
the language, "approval" changed to "approved". The Board agreed.
Planner Cronin explained a legislative change in 2025 that changed the 5-year exemption
to a 7-year exemption. Changes were made to reflect the change in state law to vesting
periods. Legal will review. Planner Cronin also updated the changes to the 65-day review
time limit, adding in the additional 30 days for developments of regional impact.
Planner Cronin pointed out in the site plan regulations where it says that all developments
must comply with the master plan. The master plan is not a regulatory document to comply
with, so she recommended removing it and adding the master plan reference to the
Purpose section. The Board agreed.
Planner Cronin struck repetitive editor's notes pointing the reader to the Zoning Ordinance.
She struck a copy and paste error. She clarified that erosion controls apply to both major
and minor site plans. There is a reference to an erosion control handbook from the 1980s.
She would like the town engineer to advise what the current industry standard is.
Chairman Seaworth suggested stating "best management practices". Vice Chair Edmonds
agreed that the town does not need to reference specific handbooks, which are
superseded all the time. The board agreed to change "best available technology" to "best
management practices"
Planner Cronin noted that there is no reference to the Floodplain Ordinance in the
floodplain section. The zoning has floodplain definitions, but not the site plan regulations.
T:\Town Planner \PLANNING BOARD\MEETING MINUTES|2026\02-24-2026 Minutes (Approved).docx
February 24, 2026 Planning Board Minutes
Page 2 of 5

She asked if the board would like to add a reference to the floodplain ordinance or not. The
board chose to leave the section as is.
Planner Cronin discussed signs. The site plan regulations say that the applicant shall
submit a sign package with their site plan application. The Board discussed the Pembroke
Crossing development. Alternate Bourque recalled that they requested more signage than
was allowed. Member Cruson felt that that location needed more signs than the sign
ordinance allowed. Alternate Bourque felt that applications should include a sign package.
Chairman Seaworth asked the board if a sign package is part of a site plan. Planner
Cronin said that in some instances it makes sense to include for design and aesthetic
purposes. She pointed out that there are instances in which a commercial building may not
have a tenant, so they would not be able to meet the requirement of a sign package. She
explained an instance in which a business wanted to put up a nonconforming sign and
argued that because they had an approved site plan, this section deemed their
nonconforming sign to be allowed. That is problematic.
Chairman Seaworth explained that ultimately it is up to code enforcement to say whether a
sign is allowed or not. If the board approves a sign on a site plan, that muddies the waters.
Member Cruson suggested adding language that final approval is by code enforcement.
Planner Cronin was more comfortable with removing the verbiage or paring it down, and
the sign permit process would determine if it meets the ordinance or not.
The Board discussed the value of reviewing signs versus not including it in the application
package and letting code enforcement handle it. The Board agreed to strike the signage
package requirement and simply state that applications need to conform to the zoning
ordinance.
Planner Cronin suggested adding two new sections: lighting and trash and refuse. These
items are on the checklist but there are no regulations currently. The proposed verbiage is
to require trash and refuse on the plan; dumpsters must be enclosed and fenced. It also
references the provisions of the solid waste ordinance, which state that commercial entities
or multifamily buildings of 6 units or more must provide their own trash service.
Member Cruson asked about businesses on Main Street that can't fit a dumpster onsite.
Selectmen's Rep Frederickson described a recently negotiated solution to allow a
business to pay a quarterly fee in advance to use the transfer station. Member Cruson
expressed issue with the language stating that "no trash shall be disposed of at the town
transfer station", when that is not the case. Selectmen's Rep Frederickson agreed that is
the case unless they get a waiver from the Select Board. Chairman Seaworth added that
an applicant can request a waiver from this item if they know they will have an issue with
trash. Planner Cronin stated that this section puts the applicant on notice that the town will
not pick up their trash. If the transfer station is negotiable, that can be amended or struck.
Planner Cronin proposed a new section on outdoor lighting to require lighting for safety
and security, aesthetics and energy efficiency (optional), and lighting shall be downcast
and not trespass onto other properties. Selectmen's Rep Frederickson asked if the zoning
ordinance addresses lighting, and was told it does not. Chairman Seaworth noted that is
why it is important to have it in the site plan regulations. The Board was not in favor of
including aesthetics nor energy efficiency in the regulations.

Planner Cronin explained that this amendment is solely to comply with a new State law.

residential unit, and Pembroke's Zoning Ordinance currently requires two. This can no
longer be enforced.
Chairman Seaworth emphasized that State law will be followed regardless of the outcome.
Diane Shuett, Pembroke Street, stated that she objects to some of the legislation put in

spoke about parking problems that may be created by ADUs. She is concerned about
narrow streets and emergency services navigating if parking is congested on the street
She noted that residents have voted many times to keep Pembroke more residential.
Chairman Seaworth feels that the Board has been sympathetic about resident concerns,
specifically as it pertains to parking. He stated that this law ties the Planning Board's
hands. He emphasized that the State law controls.
Alternate Bourque asked if Chairman Seaworth has heard anything at the State level about
this requirement. Chairman Seaworth spoke about the movement to be more development
friendly, but that there won't be as much of a push in the current legislative cycle. He does

office.

concerned about the change of characteristics of the town. She also asked if there was

PEMBROKE CEMETERY COMMISSION
October 9, 2025
Minutes
Present: Dan Chase, James Garvin, Adam Mendozza, Ellen Paulsen (chair), Zachary Sawyer,
Fleda Young.
1. Chair Ellen Paulsen called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m.
2. On a motion by Dan Chase, seconded by Fleda Young, the minutes of the meeting of
September 11, 2025, were unanimously approved as submitted.
New business:
3. Chair Paulsen distributed copies of an email report from Kirsten Rickershauser,
Children's Services Librarian at the Pembroke Town Library. In June, Ms. Rickershauser
had proposed and organized a project of placing hidden containers in one or two
Pembroke cemeteries as part of a townwide scavenger hunt connected with the library's
summer reading program for children. This would be similar to "geocaching," with clues
leading children to the general locations where waterproof containers were hidden. The
containers would contain notebooks for children to sign upon finding a cache. Following
review by the Commission and further contact with Ms. Rickershauser, Buck Street
Cemetery and Pembroke Hill Cemetery were selected to have caches hidden at or near
their front walls.
In her email report, Ms. Rickershauser stated that the program was a success. Twenty-
seven signatures were recorded, mostly from children who had followed clues to find the
caches, but with a few from those who had simply stumbled upon the caches and were
delighted to leave their names and notes. Ms. Rickershauser concluded by saying that
"we were so happy to have the support of the Cemetery Commission for this project. It
means a lot to us that our town is one where different departments and committees can
collaborate on projects like this."
Old business:
4. There has been no further discussion with private individuals who have expressed an
interest in contributing toward improvements at Evergreen Cemetery (see Item 5 in the
minutes of the Cemetery Commission meeting of July 5, 2025 and Item 4 in the minutes
of the meeting of September 11, 2025).
5. Discussions with Adam Mendozza, Public Works Department:
a. The Public Works Department received three qualified bids for tree removal and
pruning at Pembroke Street Cemetery as presented in August 2025 by Adam
Mendozza. Following discussions with V. J. Ranfos and Adam, the Commission
voted unanimously at its meeting of September 11 to recommend that the Board of
Selectmen accept the low bid of $7,200 presented by Accurate Tree Service of Bow,
N. H., to be paid from the Cemetery Capital Reserve Fund. Secretary James Garvin

2
conveyed the Commission's recommendation to Town Administrator David Jodoin by
letter on September 13, 2025. At its meeting of October 1, 2025, the Board of
Selectmen awarded the contract for tree work to Accurate Tree Service.
b. There has been no further planning for the suggested development of a spreading
garden for cremation ashes at the southeast corner of Buck Street Cemetery, an area
known to be occupied by at least a few unmarked graves of indigent persons.
c. Adam confirmed that Perry Brothers Monument Company has worked to re-set and
level the monument of Francis Garland (1917) in Pembroke Hill Cemetery. Adam
has cleaned up debris around the Garland lot.
d. Adam will clear a new area at the back of Evergreen Cemetery while carrying out a
general cleanup of the back of the cemetery.
6. Chair Ellen Paulsen reminded Commission members that veteran's flags should be
removed from the cemeteries after Veterans' Day, November 11, 2025. So far this year,
we have not had contact with Scout leaders offering to assist with the removal of flags.
Secretary Jim Garvin will inform all Commission members if he receives any messages
from Scout leaders offering their assistance.
7. The next regular meeting of the Pembroke Cemetery Commission will be at 6:00 p.m. on
Thursday, April 9, 2026, at the Public Works headquarters on Exchange Street in Suncook
Village.
8. There being no further business to be brought before the meeting, on a motion duly made
and seconded the meeting was adjourned at 6:10 p.m.
Respectfully submitted,
James L. Garvin, Secretary

New business:
3. Chair Ellen Paulsen reviewed an email she had received from Sandra Graham, who is
searching for the place of burial of a distant cousin and Revolutionary War veteran,
Benjamin Norris (1731-1799), who lived in Pembroke but is not listed among the
recorded burials in the Pembroke cemeteries. Chair Paulsen commended Commission
member Zachary Sawyer, who had researched the burial place of Benjamin Norris
immediately after receiving the meeting agenda that included Ms. Graham's question.
Zachary reported that he had used the "Find A Grave" website and had determined that
Capt. Benjamin Norris Jr. (1731-1799) is buried in Big Pasture Cemetery in Dorchester,
New Hampshire, not in Pembroke. "Find A Grave" also gave Capt. Norris' military
service and listed his wife and children. Secretary Jim Garvin will reply to Ms. Graham
with this information.

Scavenger Hunt geocache boxes that have been hidden near the front walls of Pembroke
Hill Cemetery and Buck Street Cemetery or heard any report from Kirsten Rickershauser
of the Pembroke Town Library, who initiated the geocaching program.

availability of a 14.95-acre lot adjacent to the back (west side) of Evergreen Cemetery,

PEMBROKE CEMETERY COMMISSION
April 10, 2025
Minutes
Present: James Garvin, Adam Mendozza, Ellen Paulsen (chair), Fleda Young.
1. Chair Ellen Paulsen called the meeting to order at 6:06 p.m.
2. After a brief discussion verifying that there is no reference in the minutes to scattering
cremation ashes in water, as mentioned by Colleen Russo of Buck Street, the minutes of
the special meeting of January 15, 2025, were approved as submitted.
3. Chair Paulsen reported that she had talked by telephone with Colleen Russo, who had
requested permission to purchase six adjacent lots in Buck Street Cemetery and to scatter
the ashes of family members on the surface of those lots. The Commission deliberated
upon the request in a special meeting on January 15, 2025, and sent Ms. Russo the
attached letter explaining the Commission's reasons for denial of the request. At that
meeting, the Commission agreed to explore the possibility of designating areas at one or
more Pembroke cemeteries where ashes might be scattered on the surface of the ground.
The Commission continued the discussion of possible areas for scattering ashes. Adam
Mendozza mentioned the possibility of allowing the scattering of ashes in the lightly
wooded rear right-hand (northwest) corner of the open (mowed) area of Evergreen
Cemetery. He also reported that he and Superintendent of Cemeteries V. J. Ranfos had
discussed the possibility of designating the southeast area of Buck Street Cemetery,
which until recently has been covered with white pine seedlings, as an area for scattering
ashes, perhaps marking that area with posts or a fence.
The Commission agreed to evaluate the larger wooded rear (western) area of Evergreen
Cemetery further, considering the possibility of clearing the woods of obstructions and
creating safe routes of foot travel for access to scattering areas. It was noted that such
improvements might make an appropriate Eagle Scout project.
4. The Commission further discussed the possibility of studying the acquisition of the
wooded lot south of Buck Street Cemetery as a site for surface scattering of sashes. This
lot (Pembroke Tax Map #870-0023) is presently owned by the State of New Hampshire
and administered by the Fish and Game Department. It is 1.8 acres in area and is partly
protected by the Shoreline Protection Act because it borders the Suncook River.
Secretary Garvin noted that the Cemetery Commission had inquired years ago about
acquiring this lot for expansion of Buck Street Cemetery. He suggested that if the state
should be willing to dispose of the lot as surplus land and if the Pembroke Conservation
Commission were willing to administer it as a town-owned parcel, it might be possible to
designate Lot 870-0023 as an area for scattering ashes. The Commission authorized
Garvin to contact the Conservation Commission to learn if they would be interested in

2
managing the parcel as conservation land if the state is willing to transfer the parcel to the
town.
5. A further question arose as a result of Ms. Russo's request: whether it is necessary to
revise Chapter 155 of the Town Code to limit the number of burial lot licenses that might
be sold to a Pembroke resident and/or to specify the depth of burial of human remains,
whether cremated or a full burial. The Commission observed that a limitation on burial
license sales might be prejudicial to large families who wish to have contiguous graves.
The Commission agreed to postpone consideration of revising Chapter 155, which would
require a public hearing, until a situation arises that might require the reconsideration of a
request to purchase multiple lots. Regarding the depth of burials, Chapter 155 mandates
that lot licenses are sold strictly "for the sole purpose of a place for burial of the dead,"
and that the depth of burials is left to the discretion of the contractor who performs
interments for the Town of Pembroke.
6. The Commission briefly discussed the appropriateness of levying a fee for permission to
scatter ashes in areas that may be designated for surface deposition in the future. The
consensus of the Commission was that a small fee would need to be charged to reimburse
administrative time in scheduling and recording the scattering of ashes.
7. The Commission discussed the need to purchase flags for veterans' graves before
Memorial Day, May 26, 2025. Secretary Garvin reported that he had contacted the
American Legion Flag & Emblem Department, which provides polyester-cotton flags
with 5/16" diameter sticks that would be less prone to swell and freeze into the small
sockets of old flag holders than do the 3/8" sticks that we have previously purchased. The
American Legion requires prepayment of orders by credit card or money order. Because
the Public Works Department has no credit card, Garvin offered to order four gross of
American Legion stick flags and later request reimbursement from the town. In the
interest of replenishing our limited flag supply before Memorial Day, the Commission
agreed to this proposal.
8. The Commission returned to a discussion of the services offered by All Funeral Services,
an organization that provides full services in areas of cemetery recordation and operation,
as outlined in the Pembroke Cemetery Commission minutes of October 10, 2024. The
Commission has long included "putting the full cemetery database on the town's
website" as one of our six-year goals. The Commission discussed the possibility of
establishing a designated town account to pay for this project, perhaps allocating a
portion of our yearly Cemetery Capital Reserve Fund appropriation for that purpose. The
Commission asked Secretary Garvin to review the information he received at the 2024
All Funeral Services webinar that he attended on behalf of the Commission and try to get
estimates for the specific services we would need to "put the full cemetery database on
the town's website."

9. The Commission noted that we have not heard this year from Catrina Rantala of Suncook
Cub Scout 270 regarding the willingness of the scout dens to place flags on veterans'
graves before Memorial Day, May 26'h. Secretary Garvin will contact Ms. Rantala to
assure her of the Commission's willingness to accept the scouts' help.
10. The next regular meeting of the Pembroke Cemetery Commission will be at 6:00 p.m. on
Thursday, May 8, 2025 at the Public Works headquarters at 8 Exchange Street in
Suncook Village.
11. On a motion duly made and seconded, the meeting was adjourned at 7:00 p.m.
Respectfully submitted.
James L. Garvin, Secretary
