BOARD OF SELECTMEN
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
September 24, 2025 at 6:00 PM
Present: Selectman Matt Miller, Selectman Karen Yeaton, Selectman Bryan Christiansen,
Selectman Sandy Goulet
Excused: Selectman Rick Frederickson
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:02pm.
II.
Citizens Comment
None
III.
Scheduled Meetings:
Chief Paulsen - Turnout Gear
Chief Paulsen stated that they are looking to replace an additional 5 sets of turnout
gear out of the 2025 operational budget. The Department has already purchased 12
sets and received notice in August from Bergeron Protective Clothing, the current
vendor, that the order is finally being put into production. Bergeron Protective
Clothing quoted $16,436.44 for 4 additional sets. Chief Paulsen also reached out to
Fire Tech & Safety and was quoted $16,180 with an 8-10-week delivery time. They
are requesting the Board waive the three competitive bids requirement.
Selectman Goulet asked why they are only purchasing four sets instead of the five
originally budgeted. Chief Paulsen stated that they will likely purchase the 5'' set at
the end of the year if the budget allows.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to waive the 3-bid requirement and to proceed with
purchasing from Fire Tech & Safety in the amount of $16,180. Selectman Miller
seconded the motion. Motion passed 4-0.
Selectman Miller asked if the specs and cost were consistent with the original order.
Chief Paulsen explained Fire Tech & Safety is able to match the design and quality.
Chief Paulsen - Update on Memorial Park Hydrant

Pembroke Water Works and the Pembroke Fire Department have collaborated on a
project that will allow the Fire Department to train utilizing a special hydrant fed by
the Merrimack River in Memorial Park. They purchased some of the supplies and
materials with the assistance of Pembroke Water Works and after further review of
the list of materials and the location, they identified that they need an additional 60
feet of pipe and fittings. The additional funds would come out of the 2025 training
budget.
Assistant Chief Farley explained the PFAS contamination of one of the wells caused
Pembroke Water Works to cancel the use of any town hydrants for training. This
hydrant will allow them to do training independent of the municipal water system.
They tried to ensure the hydrant is not intrusive of the park.
Chief Paulsen - Update on Disposition of Property
At the August 20 meeting the Board approved disposition of various items to St Jean
Auctions. The original understanding is that the auction house would come pick up all
of the items but there were some items they were not interested in. Those items will
be taken to the state for the October 18" auction.
Chief Paulsen - 2026 Budget Presentation
Chief Paulsen reviewed the increases and decreases in the Pembroke Fire Department
2026 Budget:
• Wages - 1.88% increase
• Social Security and Medicare - 5.23% increase. These are both a formula
derived from wages.
• Fire and EMS Training - 46.79% decrease. The training was budgeted at a
higher rate than they are being charged. Selectman Yeaton asked if they
are cutting back on training because the budget to actuals for the past
several years has been less and less. Chief Paulsen stated they are not
cutting back but there has been an issue with the availability of Fire One
classes. The cost of the classes has significantly decreased as well. The
Department holds a large amount of training in-house and that is not
reflected in the budget lines. Selectman Goulet asked if they collaborate
vith other agencies for training like the Police Department does. Chie
aulsen stated they have done some mutual aid trainings and hel
trainings with the area compact.
•
Dispatch Fee - 2.06% increase. It is contracted service
Testing - 35.52% decrease. Some of the testing was able to be completed
this year and does not need to be added to next year's budget. Some
testing of equipment was moved to Equipment Maintenance & Repairs.
Selectman Yeaton noted that the actual budget spent for the last 3 years
has been under what is budgeted by a significant amount. Chief Paulsen
stated that the numbers he has in this year's budget he is confident on.

• Dues & Subscriptions - 64.21% decrease. NFPA changed the subscription
model, so dues are attributed to one person vs. being department wide.
• Fire and EMS Supplies - 10.97% increase. Selectman Miller asked if the
supplies such as class a foam has a shelf life and what is the procedure if
they expire. Chief Paulsen stated they cycle through the foam on a regular
basis, so they have not encountered any shelf-life issues.
• Postage and Gas & Fuel lines remain unchanged. Selectman Yeaton asked
if the actual to date of $1,156.78 is correct. Chief Paulsen explained they
are purchasing diesel through State of NH and the actual is higher. David
shared they paid the invoices with the State, there was a billing error on
their end, they returned the checks to the Town, and the Town had to
reissue. The actual to date is around $3,300 higher but it was not reflected
when this report was made.
• Safety Equipment Purchases - 12.59% increase. Next year they are
looking to replace 6 sets of turnout gear. Which makes up $24,600 of the
budgeted amount. Selectman Miller asked why there is such a large
difference on the budget to actual over the past three years. David
explained they hold off on their purchases until the end of the year and
then it is encumbered and shown in the audit. It does not appear on this
report.
• Equipment Main & Repairs - 39.07% increase. Some standard equipment
testing has been moved from the testing line to this line as well as some
annual preventative maintenance items. Selectman Yeaton asked if there
are still expenses to come out of the year-to-date number. Chief Paulsen
stated there is yearly SCBA testing and that will consume a lot of the
balance.
•
New Equipment - 28.55% decrease.
Replacement Equipment - 243.22% increase. This will replace thermal
imaging batteries, 4 gas meters, stream light hand lights, Stil chainsaw,

POLICY
1. General Policy:
a. Tri-Town EMS shall bill for EMS services rendered

b. Balance Billing: The Service or its billing contractor, shall submit a bill to the

third party payer (insurance), except when legally or contractually prohibited to

c. Tri-Town EMS shall not attempt to collect a balance on an account, after an

d. Tri-Town EMS shall contract with an outside agency for the purpose of billing for
and receiving revenue associated with EMS services that result in a patient
transport.
Tri-Town EMS shall be responsible for submitting invoices and receiving revenue
that is the result of special events where EMS standby services were requested
and given and for Paramedic Intercepts with other EMS agencies. The Service

BOARD OF SELECTMEN
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
September 3, 2025 at 6:00 PM
Present: Selectman Matt Miller, Selectman Karen Yeaton, Selectman Bryan Christiansen
Excused: Selectman Rick Frederickson and Selectman Sandy Goulet
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
I.
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:00pm.
I. Citizens Comment
VJ Ranfos, 307-323 Third Range Road, purchased property on the Range Roads and
there is a large mud puddle making access difficult. VJ is asking permission from the
Selectboard to dump some rock on the road where the puddle is located to make
access easier to get to his property.
Selectman Miller clarified that VJ would be purchasing the stone and completing the
maintenance on his own. VJ explained that he is purchasing the stone himself and
using vehicles that are not town owned vehicles.
Selectman Yeaton asked Adam Mendozza if there are any concerns from DPW.
Adam answered there are not.
Selectman Christiansen made a motion to allow VJ Ranfos to put stone at 307 Church
Road at his cost. Selectman Miller seconded the motion. Motion passed 3-0.
Ill.
Scheduled Meetings:
Chris Gamache - Collections Policy
Chris Gamache, EMS Director, stated that as of August 1, 2025, there is $148,903.85
in collectibles waiting for disposition. The bulk of that is from ambulance runs in
2024 but some is from early 2025. They should expect to see about that amount on an
annual basis. They received $185,455 in revenue from 2024 runs which is 68.25% of
what they would expect from ambulance billing. Historically, that is a little low but it
is in the ballpark of what they would expect to see. Some payments are continuing to
trickle in from payment plans but the vast majority of accounts are closed out. The
service brought in around $740/per transport which is higher than they have
historically seen. When looking at 2025 runs, the service has received $173,000

Selectman Yeaton asked how many accounts the outstanding $148,903.85 represents.
Chris answered it is about 100 and each account is a separate run since they are billed
separately so it could be the same person. Selectman Yeaton asked how the 100
accounts compares to the number of accounts in the same time period. Chris
answered it is about a 1/5 or 20%. Selectman Yeaton asked if that is typical. Chris
answered that it is what they have been seeing over the past 10-12 years. When
looking at the accounts with balances, they are either the Medicare allowable amount
or the full balance. There isn't much in between.
Selectman Yeaton stated the old manual that they are looking at is for Tri-Town EMS
and they didn't separate out residents vs. non-residents. In the new policy, they may
want to keep with that practice.
Selectman Miller stated it is important that people feel an ownership over their
ambulance billing and expressed concerns that he doesn't want people to feel
comfortable allowing their ambulance bills to fall on the property taxpayers just
because they can. Selectman Miller likes the layout of the policy, but it needs to be
updated to reflect Pembroke EMS and there is a lot of heavy process and would like
Chris to tell them what they could do to make the policy less of an administrative
burden. Selectman Miller shared Selectman Goulet's thoughts that there may be a
dollar threshold the Board could give the Director discretion on for collections.
Selectman Christiansen also likes the policy but has concerns about having a dollar
amount that is automatically written off rather than allowing the Director to use
discretion. They also need to change the wording from Board of Directors to Board of
Selectman which then means they need to change some of the provisions. Right now,
it states active board members do not have to pay their ambulance bills and the
Selectman should not be exempt from having to pay their bills. David stated that
Town Employees should not be exempt either unless the incident occurs while on the
job.
Selectman Miller stated that rather than looking at a Tri-Town policy and trying to
adapt it to Pembroke EMS at this meeting, Chris should take it back and revamp it to
work for just Pembroke EMS and then they can look at that and make changes.
Chris shared the viewpoint of the previous Board when the hardship process
guidelines were established was to mirror the tax abatements process. People would
either fill out the request form and refuse to give bank account information and all the
other required documents or people would show up with packets and packets of
paperwork. Selectman Miller asked if Chris could propose a change to the policy and
only ask for what is practical, reasonable, and necessary from his viewpoint.
Chris asked if they would like to break things out between residents and non-
residents. Selectman Christiansen stated he thinks everyone should be treated equally.
Selectman Yeaton proposed possibly having the primary distinction between

residents and non-residents be the amount of allowed time to contact them to either
start a payment plan or to apply for hardship. Residents could have 90 days and non-
residents could have 60 days. Chris stated that practically, by the time an account hits
disposition list, the 60-90-day time frame would be a very hard thing to put into
practice. They can look up to see when a call went out but that has no bearing on
when the billing actually happens due to how insurance billing works. They would
often consider when an account hits the disposition report as the start date to figure
out what they are going to do with it. If they wanted to give each account a different
time frame, then they would have to look at every account every month and keep
additional spreadsheets. Administratively, it would be a hardship. Chris explained if
he was to make a distinction between non-resident and resident when they hit the
report, a non-resident would be sent to collections and residents would get an
opportunity. The bulk of the disposition report is Pembroke residents.
Chris stated that he would like to have a dollar value for write offs and asked if there
is a number the Board would be comfortable with. Selectman Miller stated they need
to get the process hammered out and then from those discussions, they can come to a
dollar amount. Selectman Christiansen would like to see a recommendation from

Chris will put together a new draft of the policy to distribute to the Board for further

schedule would be $480/year for a 96-gallon container, $1,800/year for 2-yard
dumpster, and $2,700/year for a 4-yard dumpster. The fee is consistent with what
Casella would charge.
Selectman Christiansen would like to add language to say all fields on the application

BOARD OF SELECTMEN
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
August 20, 2025 at 6:00 PM
Present: Selectman Sandy Goulet, Selectman Matt Miller, Selectman Rick Frederickson,
Selectman Karen Yeaton, Selectman Bryan Christiansen
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
I.
II.
III.
IV.
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:00pm.
Citizens Comment
Sue Whitbeck,
, 343 Pembroke Street, shared that next year, the Library Trustees
would like to nominate the new librarian for Librarian of the Year. Sue is requesting
that the Board or anyone that notices anything they like or appreciate that the Library
is doing to let her know so they can put together a nomination package when the
nomination period opens next June. Selectman Miller shared that NHPR did a nice
piece on the Pembroke Library that aired on Monday.
New Business
Manifest/Abatements
Selectman Goulet made a motion to approve the manifest and abatements. Selectman
Christiansen seconded the motion. Motion passed 5-0.
Scheduled Meetings:
Conservation Commission - Lariviere Land Donation 332 Sixth Range Road
Ammy Heiser, Co-Chair Conservation Commission, would like the Board to accept
the donation of a 50-acre parcel located at tax map 262 lot 47 or 332 Sixth Range
Road. The Conservation Commission has viewed the entire property, and it rated 21
out of 27 on their criteria rating list which is very high. The Commission will pay for
the legal, appraisal, recording of the deed, and a title search. Currently the
conservation fund has $635,399.05. The appraisal will be good for 60 days and
according to the town lawyer (Steven Whitley) it will be a straightforward process,
and he does not foresee any issues. When Ammy donated 30 acres in 2019, the cost
for legal was $2,500 and the appraisal was $3,200. The Commission is expecting a
total cost of $10-12,000. The Town has the parcel appraised at $158,800 and if the
Range Roads are opened, they would expect to see the value go up. The Commission
has voted to accept the donation, and the next step is the Board of Selectmen need to
accept the donation.

Selectman Miller asked if the deed is written so it will be permanent conservation
land. Ammy explained that is the hope but for that to happen the land needs to be held
in a land conservation trust but unfortunately the companies that do that don't have
the capacity. Steven Whitley stated the second-best thing would be to add language
that says the property is under the purview of the Conservation Commission owned
by the Town of Pembroke managed the Conservation Commission. In order to
remove land from conservation, the Conservation Commission would need to vote to
get rid of it and then it would have to go to Town Meeting. Steven tries to put the
most restrictive language possible in the deeds without it being managed by a
conservation trust. Selectman Miller asked if they feel comfortable with the lot
survey. Ammy answered they do. A survey is expensive, for instance they just
surveyed the Beck property for a little over $11,000. This parcel has been in his
family for multiple generations. One side is already town owned conservation land,
two sides are town owned range roads, and the third line they feel comfortable with.
'electman Christiansen asked where the Beck property is. Ammy explained it is of
ow Lane and Donna Drive. The access point is Nadine Drive, it has a lot of abutter
and people have been getting generous with their own lot boundaries, so they have to
stay on top of it.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to accept the land located at 332 6' Range Road
from the John and Luanne Laviviere Revocable trust to be managed by the
Conservation Commission. Selectman Frederickson seconded the motion. Motion
passed 5-0.
Chief Paulsen - Disposition of Town Property
Fire Chief Erik Paulsen is seeking permission to send surplus equipment to auction
with JSJ Auctions. Selectman Christiansen asked for information on the thermal
imaging camera. Chief Paulsen explained that is the original thermal imaging
technology and is about 15 years old. It is pretty large, and the batteries are failing.
The batteries are very costly to replace. It has been replaced with something smaller
and more modern.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to allow the Fire Chief to proceed with disposing of
he unnecessary items as presented. Selectman Christiansen seconded the motion
Motion passed 5-(
Chief Paulsen - Forest Fire Warden Appointment
Chief Paulsen stated the Forest Fire Warden position is a liaison with the State to
facilitate equipment requests and maintenance of federally owned or state-maintained
property.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to appoint Fire Chief Erik Paulsen as Forest Fire
Warden. Selectman Miller seconded the motion. Motion passed 5-0.

Chief Gaskell - Request to Change Detail Rates
Chief Gaskell shared that area town departments are all increasing the officers' detail
pay rates. It is important that the Pembroke Police Department remain competitive
with detail rates as this is an opportunity for officers to make extra money outside of
overtime and in a way that does not affect the budget. Details bring in extra income
for the Town in the form of administrative and cruiser fees.
Selectman Miller asked how this rate is collected. Chief Gaskell stated this rate is
billed to anyone that needs an officer such as Lucas Trees when they are cutting near
the road. If they cannot fill the detail request, they will ask other agencies. It is for
any non-Pembroke entity.
Selectman Christiansen asked if it is in the ordinance that this is required on every
street. Chief Gaskell answered the Town does not have an ordinance that states when
a detail is required. Selectman Christiansen stated it may behoove the Town the
institute an ordinance addressing when a detail is needed.
Selectman Yeaton asked if there is a formula to determine what the rates are. David
explained that historically the average of the salary plus benefits is the hourly rate of
pay and then they have added a percentage to each on top of that. They are requesting
the officer's hourly earning rate to be $70 and the detail rate without a cruiser be
changed to $85 and $95 with a cruiser. Selectman Goulet suggests the increase be
$95 and $105 to be more in line with the surrounding communities.
Selectman Yeaton asked if this is competitive market. Chief Gaskell stated that it is
usually a safety thing in town but other entities will hire Pembroke police officers for
a detail. It is an important opportunity for officers to make extra money.
Selectman Christiansen asked if they have a minimum. Chief Gaskell answered there
is a 4 hour minimum and anything beyond is an hourly rate.

BOARD OF SELECTMEN
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
August 6, 2025 at 6:00 PM
Present: Selectman Sandy Goulet, Selectman Matt Miller, Selectman Rick Frederickson,
Selectman Karen Yeaton, Selectman Bryan Christiansen
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:00pm.
II.
Citizens Comment
None
III.
Scheduled Meetings:
Public Hearing - Public Works Request to remove $5,200 from the Town Equipment
Capital Reserve Fund to purchase a new aluminum flatbed
VJ Ranfos, Public Works Director, stated that after Town Meeting there was money
deposited in the Capital Reserve Fund for the purchase of a Ford F600 that is to replace the
older Ford F550. The cab, chassis, and plow equipment were ordered, and they have already
taken possession of the cab and chassis. The plow equipment is not scheduled to be installed
until August 2026. In order to utilize the truck that is sitting unusable at the DPW garage,
they would like to install a flatbed while they wait for the plow equipment to be installed next
year. In the CIP plan, Public Works is scheduled to purchase a new service truck with a
flatbed in 2027. The flatbed they are proposing to purchase tonight would be repurposed onto
that service truck.
David Jodoin asked if they would treat the truck before the flatbed goes on it in order to
preserve it. VJ explained that for the last 5 years they have treated every truck in the fleet
when the winter season is over in order to preserve them. Selectman Goulet asked if they
treat other town vehicles. VJ answered they do not.
Selectman Yeaton opened the public hearing at 6:06pm.
Selectman Miller shared that having the truck sit idle for a year would be detrimental to it and
the plan to purchase the flatbed early is sensible.
Selectman Yeaton closed the public hearing at 6:07pm.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to withdraw the sum of $5,200 from the Town Equipment
Capital Reserve Fund for the purchase of the new aluminum flatbed to be used on the new 1-
ton until the plow and dump body are received. Selectman Miller seconded the motion.
Motion passed 5-0.

Public Hearing in accordance with RSA 31:95 B IIII (a) acceptance of $246,513 in
insurance money for the totaled trash truck
VJ explained that the trash truck was totaled and Primex sent a payment for the claim in the
amount of $246,513. This is the salvage cost which will allow them to retain the damaged
truck and salvage any parts off it. The plan is use the funds to purchase a new 2025 Peterbilt
from Dimmick Group Peterbilt for $210,382. Sanitary Equipment would remove the body
and equipment from the 2022 truck and install them the 2025 truck along with a new
hydraulic pump and associated equipment for a total of $60,800. The Town would then need
to enter into a 6-month lease with Premier Truck Sales and Rental for a rental truck while the
new Peterbilt is being built for a total cost of $64,400.
Selectman Christiansen asked what happens to the lease cost if the truck is done sooner than
6 months. VJ stated they are taking advantage of the plan to pay the full 6-month term up
front in order to have the delivery and removal charges of $3,000 waived. If the rental
agreement is terminated early, they will receive a refund for the unused time and have to pay
back the delivery charges. It is unlikely the truck will be done earlier than expected so any
rental savings would most likely be eaten up by having to pay back the delivery charges.
Selectmen Yeaton opened the public hearing at 6:10pm.
David Jodoin asked how much they will be able to salvage from the old truck. VJ answered
that they are able to save quite a bit. For example, items such as tires, fuel tank, mirrors,
steps, doors, and the DEF system. A salvage company came and looked the truck and they
would be willing to come and pick it up once they are done with it for $6-7,000.
Selectman Yeaton closed the public hearing at 6:12pm.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to accept the $246,513 from Primex in accordance with
RSA 31:95 B III (a). Selectman Frederickson seconded the motion. Motion passed 5-0.
VJ Ranfos - Request to purchase a new trash truck
VJ stated there are a few options that they have been reviewing. One option was a chassis in
California but unfortunately that wasn't the correct fit. Another option was a rental company
out of Massachusetts that had a truck, but communication was poor and they received
unfavorable recommendations, so they decided against that company. Another rental
company, Premier, has a single body truck that is available to rent. A single body truck means
they would need to pick the route twice on Mondays and Wednesdays. They would pick up
all the trash and then all of the recycling. The white truck can assist with the longer routes on
Thursdays and Fridays. They do not pick on Tuesdays. In the past, they have had to do this
with Casella so they know it will work. They are looking to purchase a new Peterbilt and
ship the truck up to Canada to be put together with the old equipment.
Selectman Miller asked what the impact of tariffs could potentially be. VJ stated the pricing
is locked if they make the decision to go that route tonight. This option will cost in total
$335,582. The check from Primex for the totaled trash truck is $246,513 which leaves a
balance of $89,069 that will need to come out of the Capital Reserve Fund. It will require a
public hearing to withdraw the funds. David explained that since the payments can be made

in phases, they should use the Primex money to lock in the lease quotes and order the truck
and then in the meantime, hold a public hearing so those timelines aren't stressed.
Selectman Miller asked what impact purchasing this new truck now will have on the CIP
planned purchases. VJ answered it will not have an impact because they will still need a new
truck next year that will replace the spare truck. The lead time on new trucks is around 18
months.
Selectman Miller asked what insurance will be on the rental truck. VJ answered the company
has insurance on it as well as the Town.
Selectman Miller asked if they have seen effects of the accident on the insurance rates. David
answered they would not know that until January.
Selectman Frederickson asked if they have gotten quotes for a trash pick-up services rather
than purchase our own truck. David stated it was looked at last time they renewed the trash
contract with Casella. They only received one bid back. Recycling costs are up over $5/ton
and having a split body truck is more expensive and it may be time to relook at privatization.
VJ explained that Bow just signed a contract with Casella for roughly $750,000/year. Bow's
picking is very comparable to Pembroke. Pembroke's trash costs are around $600,000/year
when you split out the costs of the trucks over the years.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to allow the Public Works Director to sign the letter of
intent with Sanitary Equipment pending legal approval. Selectman Christiansen seconded the
motion. Motion passed 5-0.
Public Hearing - Request to change Town Code Chapter 160 Certified Mailing Fees
Carolyn Cronin sent a letter to the Board that the US Post Office recently increased the fee of
sending certified mail to $10.44. The Town currently charges $10 per certified letter in
accordance with the fee schedule for an application to both the Planning Board and Zoning
Board. Carolyn is suggesting the abutter fee be increased from $10 per letter to $15 per letter
so that the applicant fully covers the cost of the postage, mailing materials, and staff time.
The fee would also align with surrounding town's abutter's fees.
Selectman Yeaton opened the public hearing at 6:35pm.
Selectman Yeaton closed the public hearing at 6:36pm.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to approve the certified mail fees as presented. Selectman
Miller seconded the motion. Motion passed 5-0.
Chris Gamache -EMS Director - Financial Review; Write off Policy/Collection Policy
Chris Gamache, Pembroke EMS Director, stated June 30" marked the first full year of
Pembroke EMS operations and shared highlights from the past year:
Number of EMS Incidents 872 - projected between 800-900
• EMS Transports 479 - projected between 450-500
Runs within Pembroke 647 - projected between 600-700
• Mutual Aid Given 225 - projected between 200-300

CHAPTER 178
PURCHASING PROCEDURES
[HISTORY: Adopted by the Board of Selectmen 9-23-2002 by Ordinance No.
02-04. Editor's Note: This ordinance also repealed former Chapter 178, Purchasing
Procedures, adopted by the Board of Selectmen 9-25-1995 by Ordinance No. 95-
Amendments noted where applicable.]
$ 178-1 Payment of monies.
All expenditures in the Town General Fund shall be paid out only as authorized
by the Board of Selectmen on checks drawn by the Treasurer, or Deputy
Treasurer, in accordance with the Internal Control procedures adopted by the
Board of Selectmen. In emergency situations, approval may be obtained from the
Town Administrator for unbudgeted purchases in the amount of one cent ($0.01)
to five thousand dollars ($5,000.). Transfers may be approved by the Town
Administrator. Either of these actions by the Town Administrator is to be included
on the next manifest for Board of Selectmen review and/or approval.
§ 178-2 Use of payment vouchers.
A completed payment voucher and supporting documentation is required for all
expenditures. All requests
for payment must be submitted to the Finance
Department for processing in accordance with the Internal Control procedures
adopted by the Board of Selectmen. Only department heads, or their designees,
are authorized to make purchases on behalf of the Town up to the amount of
Tenfive thousand dollars ($105,000.).
§ 178-3 Bid process.
Purchases/repairs in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000) and over must-
be approved by the Board of Selectmen after three (3) competitive bids.
The results of the three (3) competitive bids required for purchases over fifteen-
thousand dollars-five thousand-dollars-($15,000) ($5,000) shall be submitted
to the Town-Administrator for review and submission to the Board of Selectmen
for its review and disposition. Consecutive
1

purchases from-the-same-vendor, for the-same purpose, shall be considered
to-be one purchase.
§ 178-3 Bid process. (Revised)
For all purchases or repairs of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) or more,
the following additional requirements shall apply:
1. Sealed Bids Required: All bids must be submitted as sealed bids and
opened at a public meeting or bid opening session designated by the
Board of Selectmen or Town Administrator.
2. Written Specifications: A detailed written bid specification document
must be prepared for the project or purchase, outlining the scope of
work, technical specifications, timelines, deliverables, and any applicable
standards or expectations. These specifications must be distributed to all
prospective bidders to ensure that all bids are based on the same
information and deliverables.
3. Submission and Review: The results of the three (3) competitive bids
shall be submitted to the Town Administrator for review and then
forwarded to the Board of Selectmen for final approval and award of
contract.
Consecutive purchases from the same vendor, for the same purpose,
shall be considered one purchase and subject to the same thresholds and
bidding requirements.
§ 178-4 Bid process exceptions.
No competitive bids, as called for in § 178-3, shall be required when purchasing
through the State of New Hampshire or at prices comparable to State of New
Hampshire bid prices. The requirement for three (3) competitive bids may also be
waived in specific instances by a majority vote of the Board of Selectmen. Waiver
requests must be submitted, in writing, to the Town Administrator for review and
submission to the Board of Selectmen for its review and disposition.
178-5 Request for Expenditures from Town Capital Reserve
Funds
The Board of Selectmen shall assess all requests for expenditures from Capital
Reserve Funds in a way that balances immediate operational needs with the Town's
long-term financial stability. This assessment shall follow best practices that foster
fairness, transparency, and accountability. The Selectboard will ensure that all
capital reserve fund decisions align with municipal goals, allow flexibility for
unforeseen needs, and uphold public trust through consistent engagement with
taxpayers, auditors, and the Municipal Budget Committee.

BOARD OF SELECTMEN
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
July 16, 2025 at 6:00 PM
Present: Selectman Sandy Goulet, Selectman Matt Miller, Selectman Rick Frederickson,
Selectman Karen Yeaton
Excused: Selectman Bryan Christiansen
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:00pm.
IL.
Citizens Comment
None
III.
Scheduled Meetings:
Public Hearing Town Code Chapter 178
Selectman Yeaton shared that the proposed changes to Chapter 178 updates the
purchasing procedures for capital reserve fund requests in order to ensure
transparency, fiscal responsibility, and that purchases align strategically with the 5-
10-year plans for capital expenditures.
consistency. David will make the changes once the chapter is approved
Selectman Yeaton shared some grammar changes sent via email from Gerry Fleury.
178-5 section b-2 needs to change b to be and in 178-5 section c-2 needs to change if
to whether.
Selectman Yeaton opened the public hearing at 6:05pm.
Gerry Fleury, 24 Kimball Street, looking at chapter 178-5 section 5 Accountability,
there are a number of items that would create a requirement that funding sources for
capital reserves be documented. If the Trustee of Trust Funds are doing their job, this
should already be done and is redundant. David explained that section was added for
clarity when the Boards and Trustees inevitably change over.
Selectman Yeaton closed the public hearing at 6:11 pm.

Selectman Goulet made a motion to approve Town Code Chapter 178 as amended.
Selectman Miller seconded the motion. Motion passed 4-0.
VI Ranfos - Trash Truck Update
V Ranfos, Director DPW, explained that the trash recycling truck was involved in a
crash a few weeks ago and Primex has officially totaled the vehicle. Selectman
Goulet asked if the investigation into the crash was completed. VJ answered it is not.
Selectman Frederickson asked if they have been given an amount Primex will
compensate the Town for the truck yet. VJ answered Primex has valued the vehicle at
$321,445. There is a $1,000 deductible so the payout comes to $320,445. VJ
explained the salvage value of the truck is $73,932. Selectman Goulet asked if they
were able to purchase it back, is it actually salvageable. VJ answered there is likely
front end frame damage, and the hydraulic pump was pushed up into the
transmission, so it likely has no functionality. If they purchase it back, the net claim is
$246,513. They have been looking at options to see if they can get a used chassis and
remove the body from the old truck. Peterbilt gave a quote for $229,000 for a new
chassis and the cost for Sanitary Equipment to swap the body is $57,000. To buy
brand new, the chassis is $229,000 and the body is $230,000. They need a truck as
soon as possible. If they go brand new, it will fake 12-18 months. If they buy the
chassis and swap the body, it is likely closer to 4-6 months. They found a used 2019
cab and chassis in California for $123,900 and they could add the salvaged body for a
total of $173,970 but they would need to purchase new hydraulic pump and hoses.
Selectman Frederickson asked if they are sure the body would fit the new chassis. VJ
answered the company in California took all the specs from the old truck to compare
and they would have to do some retrofitting, but it is included in the quote. Shipping
costs are around $8,000 and is also included in the $173,000 quote. They would need
to rent a truck in the meantime from Refuse Rental Specialists. They have a 12-month
rent to own option where they would take 25% of the rental costs and put it towards
the cost of the new truck. They are still working on those numbers. Selectman
Frederickson stated that with a monthly rental fee of $11,350 that's $136,200 for the
year and 25% of that does not amount to too much. VJ explained he would like to
start the rental as soon as possible because the truck they are using as a replacement is
very old and is continuing to break down so they are having to pick up trash late.
David asked why there is a 2019 chassis available right now. That is a fast return. VJ
answered there was an insurance claim for a fire on the body but the chassis was not
damaged. They removed the body and kept the chassis. VJ will work to firm up
timelines and total all in costs of each option. Selectman Yeaton would also like some
additional commentary on how these options impact the planned CIP purchase of a
new trash truck next year. Selectman Goulet would also like to see some data on the
cost of the upkeep of the old truck.
VJ Ranfos - Request to remove money from Capital Reserve Fund to purchase a new
flatbed

VJ explained that at Town Meeting, DPW was approved for a new non-cdl truck and
accessories. They have taken delivery of the chassis for the F-600 but they are still in
line and waiting until August 2026 to get the plow equipment put on. Since they have
the chassis, they are looking to utilize the truck rather than let it sit there. Viking has a
flatbed with a tie down kit for $5,200. In the CIP, the service truck is up to be
replaced in 2027. If they purchase the flatbed now, they will have the flatbed on the
new truck for a year, take it off when they get the plow equipment put on, and then
have this equipment for the purchase of the next service truck and accessories in
2027. Selectman Frederickson asked if the company can guarantee the truck in 2027
would fit this flatbed. VJ answered that he assumed the purchase in 2027 will be
another Ford F600 since they have been very happy with the Fords and that would fit
the flat bed.
Selectman Yeaton asked if we will be down a plow truck this year: VJ answered they
worked out a deal with Grappone Ford that allows them to keep the current truck until
the new one is outfitted.
Selectman Yeaton asked what the purpose is of purchasing the new flatbed. VJ
explained the truck is sitting in the garage until the plow can be put on in 2026. This
means they could use the truck to haul equipment. The flatbed is a part of the planned
CIP purchase in 2027. This means they will not need to purchase this piece of
equipment in 2027. Selectman Yeaton asked if there is a risk to the truck sitting there
being unused. Selectman Goulet answered they could end up with rats and squirrels
and critters making a home in it. Selectman Frederickson answered it's not good for
the engine to sit for a year or more.
Selectman Miller asked if they have looked at other companies to put the plow
equipment on. VJ answered they have reached out to a number of companies, and
they all have the same lead time. The company they have selected does excellent
work which is likely one of the reasons they have such a long lead time.
Selectman Yeaton asked if there is an opportunity to pay for this out of the operating
budget. VJ answered they are right on schedule with what they anticipated to be spent
at this time.
Selectman Miller asked when the chassis has to be ordered for the 2027 truck for it to
be available. VJ answered they order after they get the approval at March Town
Meeting and then they would expect it to be a few months.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to move the purchase of the flatbed to a public
hearing at the next Selectboard meeting. Selectman Frederickson seconded the
motion. Motion passed 4-0.

CHAPTER 133
SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT
[HISTORY: Adopted by Special Town Meeting 4-21-1990 Article No. I. Amendments
noted where applicable, Amended 3-12-2009 Town Meeting; Updated 5/5/14 Board of
Selectmen; Updated 11/18/15; Updated 4/7/21; Updated 5/21/2025.]
As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:
ACCEPTABLE WASTE - Household garbage, trash, rubbish and refuse originating within
the boundaries of the Town, normally collected or disposed of as a result of residential
pickups or deliveries.

BOARD OF SELECTMEN
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
July 2, 2025 at 6:00 PM
Present: Selectman Sandy Goulet, Selectman Matt Miller, Selectman Rick Frederickson,
Selectman Karen Yeaton, Selectman Bryan Christiansen
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:00pm.
II. Citizens Comment
Jocelyn Carlucci, 8 Prospect Street, explained that there is an island in the municipal
parking lot where she would like to dig out the grass, put down landscape fabric,
plant hostas, and add mulch. This island is typically very overgrown, and she has had
to ask DPW to cut the grass. Since hostas are very low maintenance and are
perennials, DPW will no longer need to mow and maintain the island. Jocelyn will
continue to weed and make sure the hostas do not overgrow the island. Selectman
Goulet made a motion to allow Jocelyn Carlucci to make over the first island in the
municipal parking lot. Selectman Miller seconded the motion. Motion passed 5-0.
III.
Scheduled Meetings:
Gerry Fleury - Solid Waste Chapter 133 Proposed Updates
Gerry Fleury, Chair of Solid Waste Advisory Committee, stated the Committee was
asked to revisit the provisions of Chapter 133 after the Town of Allenstown voted to
close their transfer station. It was discovered that local businesses from the downtown
area were bringing commercial waste to the transfer station. The downtown area has a
zoning overlay district to account for residents living above commercial properties so
they can still bring their residential trash to the transfer station. Gerry explained that it
can be complicated when business owners live above their commercial properties and
co-mingle trash. The Committee reviewed the assessment maps to look at lot
dimensions and see which properties own their land. The Committee realized there is
no way to have a dumpster on some of these lots, especially on the west side of Main
Street. There is a 4-yard dumpster behind 4 Union that is contracted by the local
businesses with the exception of Pembroke City Limits (PCL). When looking at the
property, there is no room for PCL to have their own dumpster and the owners of the
4-yard dumpster were not interested in getting a larger size and including PCL. This
led the committee to believe there is an argument for allowing an exception that
allows them to use the Transfer Station.

The proposed new language would be added to Town Code Chapter 133 Section E
"other than circumstanced allowed by Section E (2)". The Committee is then
proposing adding section E (2) to read "The Town shall not be responsible for the
transportation or disposal of solid waste (trash) or recycling from any business or
commercial sources in the Town except for the special exemptions granted in the SB
overlay of the B2 zone. Any such exemption shall be justified due to space constraints
combined with safely concerns, which prohibit the customary use of commercial
dumpster rentals. For such exemption, said business/commercial enterprises shall be
allowed access for a fee, as shall be determined and periodically adjusted by the
Town, and with written permission from the Board of Selectmen, to the Town's
transfer station during its normal operating hours. The fee assessed shall be indexed
to the Town's contractual disposal expense and use agreed upon estimates of
volume/weight of materials to be disposed of at the transfer station by the exemplion
applicant. Nothing in Section E (2) shall negate other provisions and requirements of
Chapter 133.
Gerry explained that the current tonnage fees from Casella for recycling is $120/ton
and trash is $110/ton. 23% of the waste stream is recycled material and 77% is trash.
A blended rate would come out to around $113/ton. In the Town of Pembroke, every
$100,000 spent is $.08 on the tax rate. $12,500 is a .01 on the tax rate. With the
blended rate of $113/ton, if the business accumulates 110 tons over the course of the
year, it is a penny on the tax rate. The Committee is recommending that the cost of
$113/ton be reviewed on an annual basis.
Selectman Goulet asked if DPW has any suggestions or thoughts on the fee. VJ
Ranfos stated they discussed this with Casella to see what they would charge for their
pickups for a business. They answered it would be $40/month for a 96-gallon toter
cart, $150/month for a 2-yd dumpster, and $225/month for a 4-yd dumpster. Based on
what they have seen, PCL would likely qualify for the 4-yd dumpster whereas
Jacques would likely qualify for the 2-yd dumpster. VJ would prefer to bill quarterly
of yearly to save on administrative costs and time. Selectman Goulet asked how they
would identify the people using the commercial trash such as using a special sticker.
VJ answered he has not fully thought that part out yet.
Selectman Miller clarified that they would classify these businesses once a year but
throughout the year they wouldn't monitor their use to see if they were under or over.
VJ answered they will have to apply for this so they would first have to prove they
cannot have a dumpster or trash collection on their own, and then they would
determine what type of business they are and the amount of trash/recycling they
would likely be generating, and then determine the cost based on that. They would be
billed for the yearly fee and if they feel like they are generating less or DPW feels
like they are generating more, they will adjust annually. VJ explained he would also
put the same escalator in the price that the Town pays. Gerry stated he would be
concerned that there are businesses and apartments in the area above, they could co-
mingle. VI explained they would only take into consideration the commercial trash.

Selectmen Frederickson asked if the businesses have weighed in on the fees. VJ
answered he has not spoken with any of them yet.
Selectman Christiansen stated the code should clearly state it is a yearly fee in the
ordinance.
Selectman Yeaton asked if DPW is ok with the administration of this falling on them.
VJ answered they are, and they appreciate it being an annual fee rather than a
monthly, Selectman Yeaton stated they would like to work towards having as much
documentation as possible. They would need to create application forms and have
written processes for classification as well as a process for the rate calculation.
Selectman Yeaton asked where the income would show in the budget. David
answered it would go into the solid waste budget. Selectman Yeaton asked if VJ
could anticipate any costs in administering this. VJ answered just the time to set up
the billing. Since there will be so few businesses utilizing this program, they can
simply write down the numbers of the DPW stickers that are for commercial use on a
separate list. They do not need to purchase separate stickers since each one already
has a unique number.
Public Hearing - Acceptance of Town Code Chapter 133
Selectman Yeaton opened the public hearing at 6:35pm.
Selectman Yeaton closed the public hearing at 6:37pm.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to accept the town code amended Chapter 133 as
amended. Selectman Frederickson seconded the motion. Motion passed 5-0.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to allow Pembroke City Limits and Jacques Pastry
to continue to use the Transfer Station until September 35° at which time they will
need to apply and pay the fee in order to continue to use the Transfer Station.
Selectman Christiansen seconded the motion. Motion passed 5-0.
Acceptance of Donation from Pembroke Women's Club in accordance with RSA
31:95-b III (b)
Selectman Goulet made a motion to accept the donation from the Pembroke Women's
Club in the amount of $150 on behalf of Pembroke EMS. Selectman Miller seconded
the motion. Motion passed 5-0.
IV. Old Business
Purchasing Procedures/Bids
After the Selectboard was changed to agents to expend at Town Meeting, the Board
decided they would like to adopt a Board-only policy to give more transparency to the
attendees: Selectman Bryan Christiansen Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin

Matt Petersons - Request to Waive Little League Bill
Matt Petersons, Suncook Little League is requesting the Board waive the fee for
usage of Memorial Park. This past regular season they had 225 players, 75 t-ball
players, and two tournament teams. The softball program grew from 13 players to 26
and they had 50-60 volunteers. Suncook Little League handles the mowing and
treatment of the fields at the park.
Selectman Frederickson asked how much Suncook Little League has put into the
fields. Matt explained Mowmentum charges them around $2,000 to maintain the
fields from mid-April to the end of October. Highest Grade charges around $4,000 to
treat the fields.
Selectman Christiansen asked what the league does for trash management. Matt
explained that every team picks up after themselves. They do not take care of the
town's disposal trash cans but they do take out their trash and cardboard from the
canteen and equipment rooms. They have had some complaints from the Recreation
Commission about gum wrappers, and they are working to make other coaches aware
of the issues.
David asked if they received any quotes for windows and if there is movement on the
light poles. Matt explained they got a quote for windows and it came in a little higher
than expected. They have a parent who has skyscraper glass that he is going to work
with a contractor to install in the canteen. Rose Galligan forwarded a grant
opportunity to improve lighting but he still needs to look into it. He has gotten quotes
in the past that were upwards of $120-150,000 because of the little league required

explained it would be mostly the same lights.

passed 5-0.

drampipes are a requirement of MS-4 stormwater management. A portion of the pipes
was completed in the fall of 2023, and they will be inspecting an additional 13,000
+/- feet this year using money from a grant from the Clean Water SRF. The State
requires this project to be put out to bid. Two bids came back, and they are
recommending awarding the bid to Vortex Services.

Dear, V.J. Ranfos,
RE: Plausawa Hill Road resurfacing
As we know, Plausawa Hill Road is being resurfaced. In a meeting | had with Adam
Medozza, and I believe James from Advanced Paving a month or so ago, l
expressed some concern about the absence of any slope in the cut up to our
stone wall property line, and what may be the plan to keep the road run off from
coming into our drive way.
I was told at the time by Adam Mendozza that James from Advance Paving was
the expert and he relies on him to figure this all out. I admitted that I realized that
the job was not done yet and agreed to let that work out.
It appears that they have stopped working on the road for now. I feel I need to
express my continued concern with what I see as limited options to remedy what I
see as a problem with the way the side of the road has been left in certain areas.
My first concern is the vertical cut right up to the stone wall, which at places is up
to over four feet tall. The road was paved up to a foot from this cut, leaving no
room for proper drainage or a slope of any kind that will retain some sort of slope
protection that will keep the stone wall from eventually falling into the road.
As this condition has been left, the run-off will eventually undermine the area of
the stonewall which will result in the above-mentioned issue.

This stone wall on the lower portion of Plausawa Hill Road is our property line and
it should not be disturbed.
I respectfully ask: what the plan is to do this?
Also, I wish to note that in looking at this the other day, I noticed that the
contractor had removed a surveyor's pin that was clearly marked and tossed it up
on the bank. That pin is clearly noted on a registered surveyors map, which I
believe the town has a copy of, or is available through the registry of deeds. I
would expect the contractor to have that pin re-set by a registered surveyor. I
have no idea why they felt at liberty to do that, but myself being a contractor for
50 years, I know that it is his responsibility to replace that.
As for keeping the run off from running into our driveway, I found the only thing
that worked was a water bar that I maintained at the entrance of the drive. I
assumed they would mold one in when they paved but it appears they went a
different route with a kind of speed bump. I went over this with Adam and I
believe that we left this as a work in progress.
So, back to my main concern and question is: what is the plan for this roadside
condition that would not require cutting the road back enough for a proper runoff
ditch and some sort of slope from the stone wall in the problem areas that will
retain some kind of slope protection?
Thank you for your time to consider this.
Respectfully

Selectman Miller confirmed with Poverty Plains that the Town's municipal accounts
electric supplier can continue to be Constellation Energy. He also confirmed that the
program accounts for the load the municipal accounts are using. Based on the amount
consumed, Poverty Plains would credit back to Pembroke 12.5% of the supply cost.
The current Eversource default supplier rate is around $0.08/kwh. Pembroke would
receive 12.5% of $0.08. Last year, Pembroke used around 220,000 kilowatt hours
which would mean a rebate of around $2,200. The rebate would come once a month
in the form of a bill credit or a cash deposit. The program prefers to give a cash
deposit. Pembroke has 12 municipal accounts and 7 of them are too small to be put
into the program. Those 7 comprise 4% of Pembroke's load. There is a required 12-
month termination notice unless they can find another person that could fill that load.
To apply, there is a short agreement that needs to be filled out.
Selectman Frederickson asked what the benefit of this program to Poverty Plains is.
Selectman Miller explained that the main benefit is that it helps them delay having to
build out the electric grid and generation stations. The program is to incentive the
developers and utilities to build more renewables to avoid making large investments.
Selectman Goulet expressed concerns for the length of the contract and the 12-month
lead time to break the agreement.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to authorize the Town Administrator to sign the
Municipal Host Group Net Metering Membership Agreement. Selectman
Frederickson seconded the motion. Motion passed 3-0.
Update 474 North Pembroke Road Steven Keith
David Jodoin reviewed the Selectmen's meeting recording and there are still some
discrepancies between what was said they agreed to, what was discussed, and what
could be found. At the last meeting Mr. Keith stated the he would like to have the

offer to purchase the pipe for the homeowner, they attach something to the deed that

Selectman Goulet suggests keeping everything in writing from this point forward and
if the homeowner is willing to agree to all the stipulations including purchasing the

BOARD OF SELECTMEN
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
May 21, 2025 at 6:00 PM
Present: Selectman Bryan Christiansen, Selectman Sandy Goulet, Selectman Matt Miller,
Selectman Karen Yeaton
Excused: Selectman Rick Frederickson
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
Il.
III.
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:02pm.
Citizens Comment
Steven Keith, 474 North Pembroke Road, explained the Town replaced a culvert in
between his driveway and his neighbor's driveway on North Pembroke that has
negatively affected his driveway. He appeared and told prior Boards about the issue,
and they have stated they would get him the pipe for him to install according to town
specs. He has not been able to receive the pipe. VJ Ranfos explained that in the
minutes from Roads Committee on 3/13/20 and 4/7/20, it was discussed that if the
Town was to replace the pipe, he would take care of the other improvements so he
could make his driveway wider. There are minutes in 2021 where it is discussed again
that he would extend the culvert at his expense. Steven has followed up several times
to see if DPW has had any available pipe. Selectman Goulet asked how much it
would cost to order the pipe. VJ answered $20-25/foot, and the pipe comes in 20-foot
lengths and another $30 for the coupling. Steven explained that the Town changed out
a small culvert for a larger culvert which has made the driveway narrow and there are
times he must use the neighbor's driveway to safely exit his property. Selectman
Goulet stated they will do some more research into the issue to see what is in past
Select Board minutes and David would reach out once they know more.
Scheduled Meetings:
Matt Peterson - Request to waive Little League Fees
Tabled
All States Bid - Tabled from previous meeting
Bruce Davis from All States Construction is at the meeting to discuss the increase in
cost for the asphalt rubber surface treatment planned for Borough Road that was
tabled at the last Selectboard meeting. Selectman Miller stated the Town has a 3-bid

requirement for procurement and they are trying to find the justification for waiving
the bid requirement and gain an understanding for why this treatment is priced the
way it is. Bruce explained what they do is somewhat specialized in the industry. In
southern New England, there is some competition but not in this area. They are a
contractor listed with the State of New Hampshire and they have an annual contract
that the Town can piggyback on without having to go through the bid process. The
driving cost is the asphalt cement which is the glue or binder in this treatment. In
2022, when this treatment was last used, the price went from $622/sq yd in January to
$800/sq yd in July when the project was completed. The base bid for this bid's time
frame is $650/ton which is about 11.5% over 2022 or under 3% of inflation over that
same time frame. Some of the costs are out of their hands. For example, the stones
utilized for the process are purchased from Continental Paving. They will pay
Continental $60/ton which is $10/ton over last year. That difference equates to
$.33/sq yd for this bid. There are other items used in the process that have been
subject to inflation. Selectman Miller explained that the as of the date of the bid in
2022 vs. the date of the bid in 2025, the asphalt index is up 4%. Bruce explained
every contract has an asphalt adjustment clause that allows them to adjust the price up
and down. Right now, it appears as though the asphalt index will continue on a
downward trend. The index is always low in January so waiting to put the bids out in
late April/Early May will give them more realistic pricing.
Selectman Goulet made a motion to waive the bid requirement due to a single bid and
to award the asphalt rubber surface treatment to All States Construction, Inc. with a
sum not to exceed $195,000. Selectman Christiansen seconded the motion. Motion
passed 4-0.
VJ Ranfos - Vehicle Purchasing - Pre-orders
VJ Ranfos explained that at the last meeting they discussed getting in a queue early
on in the process when ordering trucks to get on a more consistent time frame and
lock in pricing. Sean from Sanitary Equipment came to the meeting to discuss
garbage truck equipment but VJ was unable to get anyone from the cab and chassis
side to come in. The Town has it in the CIP to order a new garbage truck in 2026.
Sean explained that Pembroke gets their Labrie truck body from Sanitary Equipment
and he has seen 14-16% inflation in the last 18 months. Sanitary Equipment is willing
to lock in pricing with a letter of intent from the Town and will place the order for the
body to secure the pricing. They are willing to do this on a good faith agreement and
without a down payment. David asked what would happen if voters turned down the
funding at Town Meeting. Sean explained there is nothing binding the Town to the
equipment purchase until the chassis shows up at the factory. He is able to change
the order up until the moment he receives the chassis. If there is a change order, there
is a fee of approximately $4,000. Sean explained that Pembroke currently runs a 37-
yard, split body, side-arm truck which is the most expensive body that Labrie offers.
Locking in the rate protects the Town from inflation and on a truck that expensive,
inflation can be a lot. Selectman Goulet asked if they will notify the Town when they
are getting ready to create the chassis order or is that something the Town will need to

keep track of. Sean explained he will notify the Town prior to placing the official
order. The is no cancellation fee until the chassis is at his shop.
David asked how they would handle the bid requirement. VJ explained the last time
RPPs went out for a trash truck, they received two for the cab and chassis and one for
the equipment. Sean explained Labrie is the only one who offers the 37-yard split
body so it makes sense that the Town would only receive one bid. David asked if they
factor in tariffs since Labrie is a Canadian company. Sean explained he cannot offer
any tariff protection and cannot plan for something that is not in place. Labrie has
three factories and two are in the United States. They are working on expanding their
US factories but it will take time.
Selectman Christiansen asked how many other communities they working with and
making this offer to. Sean stated Biddeford, ME just completed the process, City of
Nashua sent a letter of intent for 7 orders, and they are working with the City of
Portsmouth for 4 units.
Selectman Goulet reiterated that if they were to get in the queue, and the voters say
no, they will have to pull the letter of intent. Sean explained they do understand that,
and the letter of intent should clearly state that. The letter of intent is not a binding
contract. Sean is willing to send examples of letters of intent.
Selectman Miller asked if Sean could explain exactly how the process works from
start to finish. Sean explained he would sit down with the Town to create a quote
with specs for the body. They will get a quote from Woodbury that is good for 60-90
days, the Board will review the quote and create a letter of intent, once that is
received, he will work on a contract with Labrie to lock in a price. The contract will
be good for about 2 years. Right now, it is taking about 300 days for the chassis to
arrive at the factory.
Selectman Goulet asked why Pembroke uses the 37-yard split-body if it is rare. VJ
explained it is the largest they offer which means they can make less trips to unload
which saves time and money.
David stated they will also need to decide on whether they stay with the split body
style or move to single stream. VJ explained that if the voters approve to put the
money in the capital reserve account and the bid goes out for the cab and chassis and
then at March Town Meeting if they decide to no longer move forward with the
recycling program, they can make the change to a single unit, but it will cost $4,000
for the change order. A single body trash truck is roughly $30,000 less expensive than
a split body, so the Town is still saving money.
VJ will gather copies of the letter of intent and bring them back to the Board for
further discussion.

TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH

Selectman Sandy Goulet, Selectman Matt Miller
Staff: Town Administrator David Jodoin
Call to Order:
Chairman Yeaton called the meeting to order at 6:0pm.
IL.
Discuss Best Practices for Purchases
Selectman Yeaton explained this initiative was driven by the voters electing the
Board of Selectman to be agents to expend on all capital reserve fund accounts except
for the Sidewalk Improvement Capital Reserve Fund and the Recreation Capital
Reserve Fund. Selectman Yeaton created a document to pull together best practices,
mostly with the focus being mostly on how to manage unplanned purchases. The CIP
process will still be important and a part of the annual budgeting process. Any
purchase not included in the CIP process will be considered an unplanned purchase.
Steps for an unplanned purchase:
• Set a clear criterion would be to assess the urgency of the purchase. Requiring
the department heads to evaluate the urgency prior to coming to the Board.
• Exhausting alternative funding sources
• Asking department heads to demonstrate an alignment with strategic, fiscal,
and long-term goals.
Financial impact assessment
Transparent Communication
•
Following existing bidding process rules
•
Evaluate the amount of unplanned purchases
Selectman Frederickson shared that he agrees with what is outlined in this document
of best practices and the guidelines are something that is important for Boards to
have. Unplanned purchases happen and sometimes purchases have to be moved up so
guidelines can be very important.

Selectman Christiansen shared the concerns heard at Town Meeting about voters not
approving purchases. They should try to over communicate when it comes to
expenditures. Selectman Goulet asked what will qualify as a purchase and would
employment benefit qualify. Selectmen Yeaton stated this document addresses
purchases that would come from a capital reserve fund so employment benefit type
expenditures wouldn't count but it would be good to outline what a purchase is.
David Jodoin stated it is important that they stay consistent with the process from
start to finish regardless of department. Anything over $5,000 triggers the bidding
process. This policy should address planned and unplanned purchases and also
address if three bids do not come in or cannot be acquired, what happens next.
Selectman Yeaton stated having these guidelines in place will help the department
heads come prepared to the meeting to discuss why they could not get three bids and
then a determination could be made about waiving the requirement rather than putting
off the expenditure while more information is gathered. David discussed having
departments heads come prepared with historical data on items like a chip seal bid so
they can clearly state whether the price is the same or has gone up a certain percent.
Selectmen Goulet shared they need to be more engaged in the process from the time it
hits their packet.
Fire Chief Paulsen stated he has been having discussions with his people about being
more prepared when they come to the Board or Town Meeting in the interest of
transparency. Selectmen Goulet asked Chief Paulsen if the historical information is
available to him as a new Chief. Chief Paulsen stated they may need to do more
research, but the information exists in meeting minutes and old invoices.
Alex Marrion asked if every project must go out to bid or will they accept several
quotes. David explained anything over $5,000 must go through the bid process. Alex
asked what they would do in an emergency situation such as a truck repair or culvert
wash out. David answered he would need immediate notification explaining what
happened and why it couldn't wait so he could notify the Board.
Selectman Frederickson asked for clarification on the difference between a quote and
bid. David answered they are basically the same.
Selectman Miller asked if $5,000 is still the right benchmark to trigger the three-bid
process. Selectman Christiansen suggested polling area towns to see what they are
doing. David shared that any purchase over $1,000 must be approved by the Town
Administrator and they do not do bids for legal or the audit. There are also some
annual maintenance/repair items that do not go out to bid.
Selectmen Christiansen stated there are two different topics, CIP purchases from
capital reserve funds and department purchases and suggested that when practical, a
public hearing will be held for CIP purchases. David answered he does currently hold
public hearings for large CIP purchases such as an ambulance. Selectman Miller
agreed they should continue to have public hearing for large CIP purchases from

capital reserve funds. David explained the full CIP process should still be held for
anything out of capital reserve funds. This policy will work in tandem with the CIP
report.
1. Selectman Miller suggested there should be different types of record keeping
depending on the type of expenditure. It may not be necessary to keep a full history
on a fire truck that is purchased once every 25 years but keep only basic records on
items such as tires that are an expensive consumable that are currently purchased
every year. The reason for the difference is that an infrequent, expensive purchase
may have requirements or situational considerations that became forgotten over time
and need to be reviewed and updated when the time comes to make the next
replacement purchase.
Selectman Christiansen stated the policy should say capital reserve fund requests and
remove unplanned purchases verbiage from the whole document. Selectman
Frederickson agrees that we need to treat all purchases the same and raise the three-
bid threshold.
David suggested changing the existing ordinance to incorporate the new Board
policy.
The Board discussed the use of public hearings. The Board discussed using language
that says "when practical" versus a "must" in cases of an emergency or a decision has
to be made quickly. David stated anything non-emergent that comes out of capital
reserve fund should have a public hearing regardless of amount. Selectman Goulet
suggested using "when practical" because otherwise they need to define an
emergency. Selectman Christensen stated "when practical" leaves some wiggle room
for emergencies. Selectman Miller stated purchasing equipment should not qualify as
an emergency. Having to use culvert funds because something burst and people
cannot get home is an emergency. Language could be added to differentiate between
capital reserves that would have qualifying emergencies. Selectman Christiansen
stated the agents to expend argument at Town Meeting was so that if they needed to
purchase things quickly, they could. If they start disallowing flexibility, it could be
counterproductive of the original argument. They cannot foresee everything that
would qualify as an emergency. Selectman Miller shared concerns that adding a
broad emergency clause allows for misuse by future boards to forgo public meetings.
They could define an exemption for emergencies.
Selectman Yeaton shared preferences for this being adopted into the town code, with
public hearings as a requirement, and a very well-defined escape clause for
emergencies. The Board agrees with this as well as adding the bid process to be
sealed and a new threshold above $5,000.
David Jodoin explained that for sealed bids, they will typically set a date and time
that they are to be opened so that there is transparency for the vendors and show there

TITLE III
TOWNS, CITIES, VILLAGE DISTRICTS, AND
UNINCORPORATED PLACES
CHAPTER 31
POWERS AND DUTIES OF TOWNS
Miscellaneous
Section 31:95-b
31:95-b Appropriation for Funds Made Available During Year. -
I. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any town or village district at an annual meeting may adopt an article authorizing, indefinitely until
specific rescission of such authority, the board of selectmen or board of commissioners to apply for, accept and expend, without further action by the
town or village district meeting, unanticipated money from the state, federal or other governmental unit or a private source which becomes available
during the fiscal year. The following shall apply:
(a) Such warrant article to be voted on shall read: "Shall the town (or village district) accept the provisions of RSA 31:95-b providing that any town
(or village district) at an annual meeting may adopt an article authorizing indefinitely, until specific rescission of such authority, the selectmen (or
commissioners) to apply for, accept and expend, without further action by the town (or village district) meeting, unanticipated money from a state,
federal, or other governmental unit or a private source which becomes available during the fiscal year?"
(b) If a majority of voters voting on the question vote in the affirmative, the proposed warrant article shall be in effect in accordance with the terms of
the article until such time as the town or village district meeting votes to rescind its vote.
II. Such money shall be used only for legal purposes for which a town or village district may appropriate money.
III. (a) For unanticipated moneys in the amount of $10,000 or more, the selectmen or board of commissioners shall hold a prior public hearing on the
action to be taken. Notice of the time, place, and subject of such hearing shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the relevant
municipality at least 7 days before the hearing is held.
(b) The board of selectmen may establish the amount of unanticipated funds required for notice under this subparagraph, provided such amount is less
than $10,000. For unanticipated moneys in an amount less than such amount, the board of selectmen shall post notice of the funds in the agenda and
shall include notice in the minutes of the board of selectmen meeting in which such moneys are discussed. The acceptance of unanticipated moneys
under this subparagraph shall be made in public session of any regular board of selectmen meeting.
IV. Action to be taken under this section shall:
(a) Not require the expenditure of other town or village district funds except those funds lawfully appropriated for the same purpose; and

(b) Be exempt from all provisions of RSA 32 relative to limitation and expenditure of town or village district moneys.
Source. 1979, 42:1. 1991, 25:1. 1993, 176:3, eff. Aug. 8, 1993. 1997, 105:1, eff. Aug. 8, 1997. 2005, 188:2, eff. Aug. 29, 2005. 2014, 237:1, eff. Sept.
19, 2014.

VJ Ranfos Public Works - Chip Seal Bids
VJ Ranfos explained this type of treatment was put on Cross Country Road and it has
held up so they are going to put it on Borough Road from North Pembroke Road to
Clough Mill Road, Beacon Hill Road, and Brush Road. All States Construction was
the only company to answer the RFP with a price of $5.55/sq yd and a total cost of
$185,153.55 with a provision that if additional crack sealing is needed, that it will be
an additional $8,000.
Selectman Miller asked how the pricing compares to last year. VJ answered that it is
similar, but he will need to look it up after the meeting to be exact.
Selectman Christiansen asked what work was already completed on Borough Road.
VJ answered they have put a shim layer of asphalt on the majority of Borough and are
now looking to add it to the section from North Pembroke to Clough Mill. They will
also repair anything that was damaged over the winter before they put the surface
treatment down.
Selectman Yeaton asked if Allstate did the work on Cross Country Road. VJ
answered they did, and it has held up really well. Selectman Yeaton asked why VJ
thinks they are not receiving more bids. VJ answered it is a relatively new type of
treatment for this area and most of the companies are further south.
Selectman Miller stated he would not be in favor of waiving the bid requirement until
he is comfortable that the price increase is not outside the rate of inflation. David
stated that for the Cross Country project, the cost was $121,454.07 but they would
need to break that down by feet to figure it out the apples-to-apples cost. Selectman
Yeaton supports waiting to make this decision until they can do their due diligence of
the price increase.
Selectman Frederickson made a motion to table the chip seal bid until May 21, 2025.
Selectman Christiansen seconded the motion. Motion passed 4-0.
VJ presented the contract from KV Partners to fulfill the landfill post closure
monitoring requirements for the State of New Hampshire. It is a 1-year contract for

IV.
$6,500. This work is covered under the environmental monitoring portion of the
Public Works budget
Selectman Miller made a motion to authorize the Public Works Director to sign the
contract with KV Partners for the landfill post closure monitoring. Selectman
Frederickson seconded the motion. Motion passed 4-0.
VJ presented a list of items to bring to the St. Jean Auction that is taking place this
weekend.
Selectman Christiansen made a motion to bring the noted items to auction. Selectman
Frederickson seconded the motion. Motion passed 4-0.
Old Business
2025 Tax Deeds (2022 Delinquent Taxes)
David stated the tax deeding date is May 9, 2025. The residents on the list have until
then to pay their past due amounts or enter into a payment plan.
The list is down to one property that is for a mobile home. The park has also issued
them an eviction notice. David suggests waiting to see what happens with the eviction
before deeding the property.
Deed Waivers
David explained the deed waivers are for contaminated properties and properties with
known deed issues. One of the properties is the ally way between Jacques and
Famous Pizza. It can be very expensive to do the deed research, so they issue deed
waivers instead. Selectman Miller suggested walking some of these properties to see
if any of them would be worth putting the money into researching. David explained
the Webster Falls property has a collapsed pipe which could cost upwards of
$100,000 to fix. The THC Realty Trust property used to have barrels of unknown
material that would need to be tested. There are known contamination issues with a
lot of the properties that the Town does not want to take over: Selectman Miller will
work with David and Public Works to look at the properties over the next year.
Selectman Frederickson made a motion to authorize the tax deed waivers for tax map
266-27-2, VE-15-1, VW-114-1, VE-179-2, and VE-179-1. Selectman Christiansen
seconded the motion. Motion passed 4-0.
