Zoning Board Applications: None
Planning Board Applications:
1. Minor Subdivision Application #25-01: All-Pro Wall & Ceiling Systems, Inc, Tax Map 266,
Lot 20 located at 214 Pembroke St. in the Medium Density Residential (R1) Zone and the
Architectural Design (AD) Overlay. The Applicant proposes to convert a recently constructed
duplex into condominium ownership. Since no physical changes are proposed to the site the CC
has no comment on this application.

2. Major Site Plan Application #25-101 and Special Use Permit Application SUP-AC #22-
307: Chad Branon, MJ Properties NH, LLC, Tax Map 266, Lot 117 located at 109 Wilkins Ave.
in the Medium Density Residential (R1) Zone, the Business/Residential (B1) Zone, the Wetland
Protection (WP) Overlay, the Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Overlay, and the
Aquifer Conservation (AC) Overlay. The Applicant proposes to construct a multifamily
development consisting of two 6-unit buildings, with associated parking and stormwater
management, to be served by town water and sewer. The Applicant requests a Special Use
Permit in accordance with Article 143-68.E., Aquifer Conservation District, for residential use
over the aquifer.
Stormwater is the primary environmental concern with this plan, as this property lies within the
MS4 Storm Water Management District for the Suncook River. The lot size is 2.73 acres with
moderate slopes draining southerly to the Suncook River. The uphill portion of the property has
soil derived from glacial till, while the lower southwest corner has fine-grained stratified-drift
(sand) deposits that are part of the Suncook River aquifer. Soil depths vary from exposed ledge
in parts of the lot to 10 feet or more at the southwestern corner.
The proposed development will create 21,000 sq. ft. of impervious area. Stormwater will be
collected by catch basins which drain to a detention basin located at the southwestern corner of
the property. The detention basin outlet structure will drain to a 15" culvert which will carry the
stormwater 190 feet down along Wilkins Ave. to a 6" culvert along Buck St. that eventually
drains to the Suncook River. The CC has concerns with the quality and quantity of stormwater
which will either be infiltrated to the aquifer or discharged in the Suncook River.
Stormwater from the site is likely to contain, at various times, deicing chemicals, petroleum
products, pesticides, fertilizer, and animal waste. The likely quantities and concentrations of
these pollutants should be assessed, as well as any pollutant attenuation capabilities of the
stormwater drainage system (for both infiltrated and discharged waters). This information will
assist the Town in meeting its MS4 management and reporting requirements.
With regard to stormwater quantity, the amount of water likely to be infiltrated on a seasonal
basis should be determined. Since the proposed detention basin, at the lowest end of the property,
lies within 20 feet of the downhill abutter's property, an assessment should be made of the
infiltration effects on the local groundwater table to verify that no adverse impacts will be
imposed on the abutter. For water discharged to the 6" culvert along Buck St., an assessment
should be made of the capacity of this culvert to carry its existing load as well as any increased
load from stormwater originating in the development. To avoid cost to the Town to upsize this
culvert, the Planning Board might require that it be done by the developer as a condition for
approval of the plan.
The CC remains concerned about the long-term maintenance of stormwater drainage systems
held by private property owners and homeowners associations. Although facilities that have been
approved by the Planning Board, and later found to be deficient, are subject to enforcement
action by the Town Code Enforcement Officer, no routine inspection and enforcement programs
take place after initial approval. The loss of capacity or total failure of these systems is likely to

impose significant future costs to the Town to remedy impacts on downstream infrastructure and
water quality.
DES Letters and Applications: None.
Conservation Lands:
1. White Sands: The Town had previously requested Eversource to replace the missing lock on
the gate in the right-of-way through White Sands. During a recent inspection Erin found the gate
wide open and still without a lock. She contacted Tom Davis at Eversource. There was
apparently some confusion between the gate along their access road and the gate through White
Sands. Eversource will follow up on this.
2. Beck Survey: Ammy called Jacques Belanger to request the GPS data for the boundary
points. Jacques asked that we provide him with the data format we needed. Brian emailed
Jacques on January 13 requesting that the data be provided in gpx format.
3. Ames Brook/Adopt-a-Spot: At our December meeting, Brian agreed to prepare a draft
Agreement between the CC and the abutter regarding maintenance of the meadow areas at Ames
Brook. Karen suggested that this action could be folded into the Town's new Adopt-A-Spot
program. Brian adapted the program materials that Karen provided to fit the type activities that
the CC has considered for volunteers on conservation areas. Drafts of proposed "Adopt-A-
Conservation Area" materials were circulated to CC members by email on December 28.
The Program Description lists the types of maintenance activities grouped by increasing levels
of complexity and the knowledge and experience that would be required by the volunteer.
The Volunteer Agreement is a template form that is completed together by the CC and the
volunteer. The completed and signed agreement defines the location, scope, and frequency of the
work to be performed, and the tools and materials that are permitted to be utilized. The package
also includes the necessity legal forms for indemnity/waiver of liability that was developed for
the Adopt-A-Spot program.
Wendy, who has had a lot of experience working with volunteers at the Forest Society,
recommended excluding any boundary maintenance activity that would normally be performed
by a licensed surveyor, such as placing monuments or painting and blazing the boundary. She
emphasized the importance of CC instruction and oversite for numerous activities, such as the
identification and eradication of invasive plants. She also questioned whether volunteers should
be allowed to utilize hazardous power tools such as chainsaws. Brian agreed to prepare a second
draft to better define CC instruction and oversite responsibilities and the training, experience,
and/or licensing necessary for volunteers who propose to engage in more hazardous operations.
4. Brittany: A resident near the Brittany parcel expressed concern that "private property' signs
had been placed on the conservation area. Erin followed up by visiting the site on January 12.
She observed that the signs were on private property, significantly distant from the conservation
parcel. She informed the resident of her findings.

1. Major Site Plan Application #26-102 and Special Use Permit Application SUP-AC #26-301,
Sheep Davis Realty, LLC, owner of Tax Map 561, Lot 11-1 located at 103 Sheep Davis Rd. in the
Commercial/Light Industrial (C1) Zone and the Aquifer Conservation (AC) District.
The Applicant proposes to construct a commercial wood processing yard with associated access,
parking, and site improvements and requests a Special Use Permit for construction over the aquifer.
The CC's primary concern is any activity on the site that could impact the water quality in the Soucook
River aquifer which is used as a drinking water supply for the Town. The applicant has stated that "The
operation does not involve the use, handling, or storage of chemicals... and no activities associated with
the use are expected to introduce pollutants or increase the aquifer's susceptibility to contamination."
We note that a significant portion of the property will be paved to accommodate truck traffic, parking,
storage and processing areas. An infiltration basin will be constructed to compensate for the increase in
impervious area on the site.
The CC has the following questions that should be addressed by the Applicant: The applicant's engineer
stated that "The cordwood processing area will feature a kiln and a tumbler for treating the wood." Does
'treatment' involve more than drying? What is the tumbling process for? What will be used to power the
kiln and tumbler? If other than electric power is proposed, what measures will be undertaken to avoid
site contamination? What is the plan for sanitary waste from the site? What assurance will be provided
that the infiltration basin will be maintained in the long term?
2. Conceptual Plan, Pembroke Meadows, LLS, owner of Tax Map Tax Map 264, Lots 4 & 7; Map
266, Lots 25-4 & 26; and Map 567, Lot 1 located at 240, 274, and 282-284 Pembroke Street and
108 Broadway in the Medium Density Residential (R1) Zone, the Municipal Separate Storm Sewer
System (MS4) Overlay, the Aquifer Conservation (AC) Overlay, the Wetland Protection (WP)
Overlay, and the Floodplain Development (FD) overlay. The Applicant seeks feedback on conceptual
plans to subdivide the property into 93 residential lots with associated roadway and resident amenities.

The CC was provided with only an overview plan of the proposed subdivision. The proposed
subdivision will impact three minor tributaries to the Merrimack River and their associated wetlands.
One of these drainages, in the vicinity of the proposed exit onto Rt 3 near the Academy Road
intersection, does not appear to be shown on the plan. The CC is concerned that the proposed
subdivision will adversely impact the quality and quantity of water in these drainages due to the large
increase in impervious area and the discharge of nutrients (fertilizer, animal waste, etc.), pesticides, and
road salt from the developed areas to the wetlands and watercourses. Since these drainages exchange
water with the aquifer, these pollutants will be infiltrated to the aquifer as well. The plan shows no
proposed stormwater management facilities, which will be necessary for each of these three drainages.
The plan also shows a proposed 24-foot-wide 'emergency' road and sewer crossing over the wetlands
with no description as to how this will span the wetland and buffer.
The plan shows three proposed conservation lots of 4.8, 1.6, and 34.7 acres. The PB needs more
information on what the developer's plans are for these areas. Are they proposed to be deeded to the
Town? Even though the two small lots contain wetlands, they are surrounded mostly by proposed
development and are too small for the CC to effectively manage. On the other hand, the plan identifies
the 34.7-acre lot, which extends from the gas pipeline to the Merrimack River Conservation Area, as a
proposed non-buildable lot to be precluded from development and preserved in perpetuity. The CC
would like to acquire this lot for conservation because it abuts an existing conservation area, includes
the Merrimack River shoreline, and includes land proposed for the rail trail in the area. Retention of this
area in private ownership would limit public access and potentially thwart establishment of the rail trail.
Zoning Board Applications: Case 26-12-Z. The applicant is requesting a Special Exception to
expand the existing permitted limits of an excavation by approximately 15.5 acres. The property is
located at 774 Silver Hills Drive, Pembroke, NH, Map 559, Lot 12, in the C-1, Commercial/Light
Industrial district and partially in the Aquifer Conservation overlay, and is owned by Silver Hill
Development Corporation, 35 Veteran's Dr., Loudon, NH. The Zoning Board requested the CC to
provide comments on the proposed expansion in the aquifer area. The CC has no information particular
to this area. As in the past, our comments concern the potential impacts of the proposed mining
operations, and future use of the land, on the quality and quantity of water in the Soucook River aquifer,
which is a major source of public drinking water for the Town. Chapter 197 of the Town Code specifies
the Town's earth excavation and reclamation rules. Paragraph 197.11 provides operational standards that
need to be met in any expansion of excavation. Most importantly, the maximum depth of excavation is
limited to a minimum of eight (8) feet above the seasonal high-water table existing at the location. The
ZB should confirm that this requirement will be met by requiring the operator to provide a statement
from a soil scientist, certified in the State of New Hampshire, as to the depth of the water table at the
site. Beyond that, the ZB should require that all best management practices for sand and gravel
excavations, as specified by the State, should be met, particularly those dealing with potential
contaminants such as petroleum products.
NHDES Letters and Applications: None
Potential Acquisitions: DeStefano/Phipps. Ammy contacted Stephen DeStefano about conducting a

the Town assessment map and incorporate them into the Avenza software so that we can identify the
approximate boundaries in the field. This will be sufficient for purposes of conservation value rating.

availability of his tractor.

August meeting.

Other Business: Wetland Ordinance Update. Based on Bob's experience with the wide range of
applications for wetlands Special Use Permits submitted to the PB, he drafted a proposal for
management of wetlands buffers that recognizes four zones: 1. The wetland itself as fully protected; 2. A
ncroachment would be allowed by Special Use Permit when justified. Bob also suggested that th
ordinance by the City of Concord be considered in the PB deliberations. Bob advised that the PB wil
ake up amendment of the wetland ordinance in August and that a joint meeting with the CC on Augus
1 at 6:30 PM has been tentatively scheduled. Ammy requested that Bob provide copies of his buffe
zone proposal, Brian's draft ordinance, and the Concord ordinance to Carolyn and the PB as the CC's
preliminary input to the process.

PEMBROKE CONSERVATION COMMISSION
MEETING MINUTES
May 11, 2026
In attendance: Erin Insley (Co-Chair), Carol Bertsimas (Vice Chair), Brian Mrazik (Secretary), Ayn
Whytemare, Wendy Weisiger, Robert Bourque (PB Rep), Karen Yeaton (BOS Rep)
Absent: Ammy Heiser (Co-Chair)
Guests: Eric Temple, citizen; Joseph De Vuono II, property owner; Jeff Evans, Five Rivers Conservation
Trust (FRCT)
Call to Order: Meeting called to order at 7:00 PM.
Planning Board Applications: Special Use Permit Application SUP-WP #26-302, Joseph E. De Vuono
II, owner of Tax Map 266, Lot 114 located at 101 Smith Ave. The Applicant requests a Special Use
Permit in accordance with Article 143-72.D. to erect a fence, remove two trees, and landscape within the
wetland buffer. The proposed fence extension would add approximately 21 feet across the front and 36
feet down the side of the property. The lot contains approximately 2,400 sq. ft. of forested wetlands, in
the northeast corner, which are seasonally flooded. The outlet of the wetlands is controlled by a pre-
existing artificial weir structure on the property that creates a detention pond for stormwater within the
wetland area. Portions of the existing buffer area have been previously converted to lawn. Mr. DeVuono
assured the Commission that proper measures would be undertaken to avoid siltation of the wetland
during the proposed landscaping and removal of the two trees. He also agreed to avoid use of fertilizers
within the wetland buffer. With these conditions, the CC has no objection to the approval of the SUP.
NDES Letters and Applications: None
Zoning Board Applications: None
Potential Acquisitions: Gelinas Farm. Jeff Evans met with the CC to provide a status update on this 63-
acre parcel and to request the CC to provide approximately 50% of the funding for the acquisition. The
remaining 50% would be provided by an Agricultural Land Easement (ALE) grant from USDA-NRCS.
FRCT would be the easement holder responsible for monitoring compliance with the terms of the
easement. The total cost of the acquisition is not yet known, and no draft of the easement is available.
The discussion focused primarily on three issues:
1. Appraisal of Easement Value. The CC had previously agreed to set aside up to $10,000 from the
Town Conservation Fund for an appraisal of the property that is needed by all parties to determine
potential costs and proceed with grant applications. The CC has concern that the owners had previously
indicated they would like to recover most of the costs that they incurred in acquiring the property. Our
experience with previous appraisals has been that the easement value is significantly lower than that
derived from a 'highest and best use' appraisal typically used for marketing the property. Therefore the
owners expectations are not likely to be met. The CC would like assurance from the property owners
that they will accept the appraised value or refund the Town's expenses for the appraisal. Alternatively,
we would request that the owners, as a good-faith measure, declare their minimum acceptable purchase
price up front, so that the CC can determine the likelihood that the acquisition would proceed
2. Public Access: The CC recognizes that the operation of a horse/cattle farm requires restriction of
public access for operational, health and safety reasons. However, we believe that use of Town funds
requires that limited access be granted so that the public can cross the property, view the landscape, and

observe farming activities. To date we have received only vague suggestions for public access
opportunities. We expect the landowners to develop and present a definitive plan to meet this
requirement that would become part of the easement documentation.
3. Use Restrictions: The CC is seeking specificity regarding the land-use restrictions that will be
contained in the easement, including planned 'agri-tourism' uses. Jeff stated that the easement would
include the restrictions required by both NRCS and FRCT for farmlands. Jeff stated that one exception
was that the owners have requested they and their family members be allowed to operate recreational
dirt bikes on the property for the duration of their ownership. The CC discussed whether such a
provision would be consistent with the purposes of the easement and the potential for public objection to
such uses for which public conservation funds will be used. Several CC members objected to the
inclusion of such a provision.
Jeff agreed to discuss the CC's concerns with the property owners and to meet with us again at the June
meeting to discuss how they wish to proceed. Karen suggested that the CC develop specific criteria for
valuating proposed easements that could be applied equally and consistently to all prospectiv
cquisitions. This would be similar to the conservation value assessment that we currently use, but als
contain any considerations unique to easements.
Conservation Lands:
No new activity since the April meeting.
Eric Temple reported that he observed possible timber trespass in several locations along the Range
Roads including the Whittemore Town Forest. He observed several instances of a vehicle pulling a
trailer entering the Range Roads during the winter road closures, usually on weekends at night during
rain. The perpetrator allegedly removed large quantities of dead hardwood but also cut living trees to
gain access. Eric provided pictures of cleared areas, litter left behind and road damage. He agreed to
contact the Pembroke Police via the Resource Officer at the school where he works. The CC thanked
Eric for reporting the incidents. Ayn agreed to contact NH Fish and Game to see if they could follow up
on violations.
Review and Approve Minutes of April 13, 2026 Meeting: Bob moved to accept the minutes, as
drafted. Carol seconded. All voted in favor except Brian, who abstained.
Other Business:
1. Wetland Ordinance Update: Discussion tabled until the June meeting.
2. Private Property Signs near Merrimack River Conservation Area. Erin will contact Eversource
again to try to get more information on their right-of-way, ownership and access provisions.
Mail and Correspondence: None of significance.
Adjournment: By consensus, the meeting was adjourned at 8:55 PM.

BUDGET COMMITTEE
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
December 18, 2025
FINAL
Video recordings of Budget Committee meetings can be found at:
https://townhallstreams.com/towns/pembroke_nh
The relative start time of each agenda section is noted below.
Mark LePage, Chairman, called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
I.
Attendance
Bei, Concare, Brian earth Gene Gaus asy, Caine Hanson, Mat Mille, Kristopher Detorme, Mariana
Budget Committee Excused: Sue Whitbeck
Budget Committee Not Present: None
II. Town Budget Review - Sewer & Water Department
Kevin Brasley, Commission Chair of Pembroke Water Works, and Matt Gagne, Superintendent of Pembroke Water Works,
were in attendance to present the 2026 Pembroke Water Works Budget. Ed Lavallee, Bruce Kudrick and Lawrence
Plourde, Commissioners, we also in the audience.
Chairman Brasley explained the process the Commission uses to budget. They take the previous 11 months, multiple by
12 and apply a flat increase of 4%. Then, adjustments are made either up or down as appropriate.
Superintendent Gagne stated that there will be an increase in base rates for the upcoming year, which is primarily on
commercial use. This is for feed lines two inches or larger. There is no increase per thousand for consumption. There will
also be an increase in late fees in penalties, which have been adjusted to be more in line with others in the state. These
increases are a result of PFAs issues.
Chairman Brasley will be looking to purchase a new backhoe. The current equipment is 25 years old. They have funding
for this available in the capital reserve.
There were some projects that were not completed this past year and there is a remaining balance of $250,000, which will
be put into the capital reserve for future expenditure.
Superintendent Gagne provided an update on the potential interconnection with Concord. This needs to be approved by
Concord City Council. There are potential interconnections into Concord from Bow, Boscawen and Pembroke. Due to
various reasons, this has not been brought to the Concord City Council yet for discussion.
Brian Seaworth asked how the revenue generated from the base fee increases would be held until it is expended.
Superintendent Gagne explained that currently, the loan for PFAs projects will be approximately $7 million loan with an
additional $3.5 million paid through a grant and forgiveness from the State. There was also PFAs litigation money
received by the State that may also go towards loan pay down in the future.
Matt Miller asked about budgeting for the projects and what happens if the Commission over or underestimates the cost.
Chairman Brasley stated that if it is overestimated, it will go back into reserves. He does not remember ever having a
deficit, but they would flex funds where necessary if this was the case.

Gerry Fleury asked about the status of FAs in Pembroke water and if the levels have increased, decreased or stayed the
same. Superintendent Gagne shared that there was a period of 7 weeks during the summer where the results were "non-
detect". It has since rebounded back to previous levels but remain under the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
guidelines. Chairman Brasley added that there really isn't any explanation.
Louis Caron asked about testing for PFAs. Superintendent Gagne explained that an approved lab is used for testing and
has been used consistently.
Mark thanked Pembroke Water Works for the work they do and the services they provide.
Paulette Malo, Office Manager of the Pembroke Sewer Commission was in attendance to present the 2026 Budget.
Paulette explained that this year, heating systems were changed in three of the pump houses. There is also a new generator
on order for the Route 3 Pump House. This will leave one more generator to be changed out which is at the 106 Pump
House.
Gerry asked about sewer capacity and Paulette stated that they can hookup to an additional 400 residences at current
capacity. Upon completion of the next portion of the upgrade in Allenstown, an additional 2000 residences can be
connected. This would be an additional 500,000 gallons per day increase.
Gerry asked about the process for new connections and who pays for the infrastructure. Paulette explained that the
developer is responsible for engineering review costs as well as the infrastructure. They are also responsible for the
maintenance in most cases.
Mariana asked about the difference in costs in each pump house. Paulette explained each, with the amount of use being
the biggest determining factor. Mark asked about the difference in maintenance, which also is impacted by the amount of
use. For example, the Bow Lane Pump Station needs grease pumped out twice per year.
Gerry asked where the grease is transported to. Paulette stated that it goes to Allenstown.
Mark thanked the Sewer Commission for all the work they do and the service they provide.
David Jodoin, Town Administrator, will be updating the Town Budget and will provide it to the Committee in January.
III. Update from School
Gene Gauss spoke about the Special School District Meeting. They would like to get ahead of the Open Enrollment
movement throughout the state. This is planned for all three schools, with Pembroke Academy having the largest capacity
to accept students.
The Public Hearing for the warrant article will be January 5, 2025. There will also be a full SAU meeting that evening.
The Special School District Meeting date has changed to January 27, 2025.
The School Board also voted to change transportation companies and have gone with Butler Transportation for the
upcoming year. This is a three-year contract. He stated that this was done due to gas surcharges charged by Dale that
would make Butler effectively the same cost, and Butler offering a standby driver to prevent unforeseen changes to bus
schedules due to call outs.
Gene added clarification on the warrant article that will be presented on Open Enrollment. The warrant will limit out of
district student acceptance to 25% of the student population. There will be a restriction on students leaving the district, but
they will have the opportunity to follow the proper channels if they choose to leave.

Matt expressed concerns about attendance and asked why the School Board has decided not to include this warrant article
at Town Meeting. Gene stated that they are hoping to get ahead of the open enrollment curve. Gene also noted the benefit
of revenue generation by taking out of district students with this revenue being used to help run the schools. He
emphasized that Pembroke students will be guaranteed a spot in the Pembroke schools.
Matt stated that his concern is a lack of attendance for the vote and a possible undesirable vote if that happens.
Louis asked if there were any estimates on how many Pembroke students may leave to other open enrollment schools.
Gene stated that this would be hard to determine, but this is also why they would like proper paperwork filed for students
to leave the district. This will help with planning.
Mariana asked if there were any pitfalls of open enrollment. Gene noted that while it would be good to have lots of
interest in Pembroke schools, it may become problematic if there are too many applications and many students need to be
denied.
Gene spoke about plans to make Pembroke a destination school but also stated that this would be a gradual
implementation. There is space but not staffing for a large increase. They also see Pembroke Academy attracting the most
students.
Louis asked how tuition is determined. It was explained that it is set at 80% of the sending district's tuition. Also, state aid
would be sent to the home district, but this would be put towards the tuition sent to Pembroke.
There was some discussion on incremental revenue that could be generated from open enrollment and managing
resources. This includes how many students can be accepted with current staffing levels.
Jason Mayeu and Kris DeLorme inquired about the determination of acceptance. This is still under consideration by the
School Board.
There were further questions about how the district will ensure that Pembroke students have a spot in the school system
with students moving in and out of town, while also accepting out of district students. This is hard to predict even as it
currently stands.
There was discussion about the upcoming vote on this article. Jason expressed that it needs to be explained thoroughly to
ensure that residents understand it. Matt also added that he does not think that it is urgent enough that it cannot wait until
Town Meeting. Gerry asked if they would bring the warrant back to Town Meeting if it fails in January. Gene was unsure
of what the course of action would be if it fails as it was not yet discussed.
The Budget Committee received the Pembroke School District Budget for the 2026-2027 School Year.
IV.
Other Business
The Budget Committee will begin reviewing the school budget at their meeting on January 8", 2026.
V.
Adjourn
Clint Hanson made a motion to adjourn at 7:50 PM. Louis seconded the motion, and it was approved unanimously.
Mark LePage, Chairman

BUDGET COMMITTEE
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
December 11, 2025
FINAL
Video recordings of Budget Committee meetings can be found at:
https://townhallstreams.com/towns/pembroke_nh
The relative start time of each agenda section is noted below.
Mark LePage, Chairman, called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
I.
Attendance
Budget Committee Present: Mark LePage, Gerry Fleury, Clint Hanson, Matt Miller, Sue Whitbeck, Kristopher
DeLorme, Mariana Beer; Louis Caron, Jason Mayeu, Kerri Dean
Budget Committee Excused: Brian Seaworth, Gene Gauss
Budget Committee Not Present: None
IL.
Approval of Minutes - November 20, 2025, and December 4, 2025
Clint Hanson made a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting held on November 20, 2025. Gerry Fleury seconded
the motion. There was a correction to the attendance reported in the meeting minutes.
The motion passed 7-0. Jason Mayeu and Kris DeLorme abstained.
Clint made a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting held on December 4, 2025. Louis Caron seconded the motion.
There was a correction to the attendance reported in the meeting minutes. There was also a correction to the MS4
reference to read the Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System.
The motion passed 8-0. Jason abstained.
Kerri Dean was not present for either vote.
III.
Town Budget Review - Police
Chief Gary Gaskell and Lieut. Dawn Shea were in attendance to present the Police Department Budget. Also, in
attendance was Chris Cunha, Patrol Sargeant.
Chief Gaskell stated that he is retiring December 31, 2025. He asked that Lt. Shea present the budget as she will be
assuming the role of Chief on January 1, 2025.
Lt. Shea spoke about training for the department, which includes mandatory training. She explained that they have shifted
$2,500 from the training line to a new line called Mental Health and Wellness. Each year, every staff member, including
non-sworn staff, is required to complete a mental health consultation. This is paid for by the Department. The intention is
to keep officers healthy both physically and mentally.
Sue Whitbeck asked if they can attend more than once per year. Lt. Shea stated that this program offers a once-a-year
consultation, but that staff can get referrals to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and health insurance covers some
of these services as well.

The line for Employment Testing was explained, to include psychological exams, drug testing, medical exams, polygraph
testing, etc. This applies to all staff. The line also includes promotional testing. Kris asked about the purpose of polygraph
testing. Lt. Shea explained that it is a requirement of Police Standards and Training and spoke about expecting integrity of
staff members.
Lt. Shea spoke about dispatch services, which are provided by Merrimack County Sherriff's Department. There was a
5.32% increase ($2,368) for a total annual expense of $46,868. Gerry asked if the Department is satisfied with the
dispatch services they are using and Lt. Shea explained that this is the only option for dispatch available, but that they
have a good working relationship with them.
Lt. Shea explained that the Department receives services from the Central New Hampshire Central Operations Unit for
free due to David Jodoin, Town Administrator, providing them accounting and tax services. This saves the Department
$3,500 annually. Gerry provided kudos to David for the savings to the Police Department.
The Fuel line was decreased by $8,000 to a line total of $26,000 based on historical data. Gerry asked what the backup
plan is if there are unforeseen circumstances. Chief Gaskell noted that they have a contract with the State if necessary to
save money.
When speaking about the Office Supplies line, Mariana Beer asked Lt. Shea about the difference between the Office
Supplies line and the Department Supplies line. There was some detailed conversation about the differences, but it was
determined that some lines need to be reviewed to ensure consistency and accuracy in reporting in the future.
Lt. Shea spoke about Vehicle Maintenance and Repair line and multiple cruisers being out of warranty currently. She also
stated that the planned cruiser is in the Vehicle Replacement line in the amount of $68,500. Gerry asked Lt. Shea if this
amount would be able to purchase to cruiser and what the time frame for delivery would be. Lt. Shea stated that she
thought this amount would cover the purchase and if they purchased it now, it would be received in March.
David spoke about replacement of radios for the Department. The Department will be discussing funding this replacement
through encumbered funds as opposed to taking it out of Capital Reserves. This would be removed from the Capital
Improvement Program (CIP) Program, as a result.
Jason spoke about actuals in the equipment lines in the three previous years. He questioned why the lines are budgeted
higher when the trend has been that they are not fully spent. He added that this happens with other lines as well in the
Department Budget.
Lt. Shea spoke about technology being used in investigations and the expensive nature of evidence storage with electronic
equipment. She added that many expenses are made at the end of the year to ensure that funding is available.
Matt Miller added that encumbrances are not reflected in the budget materials provided to the Committee. This money
could have been spent after it was encumbered. Jason acknowledged this, but thinks that for accuracy, encumbered money
should be assigned to the lines where they will be spent.
Gerry added commentary about governmental budgeting and the trust associated with it. He explained the complicated
nature of encumbrances. He feels that auditors should be looking at this, which is why he requests audit reports. Jason
emphasized his trust in the administrators but still believes that the funds could be reallocated in a more accurate manner.
Chief Gaskell provided comment on his career and the Town of Pembroke. He mentioned that he attended Pembroke
Academy, and his children have grown up here. He is proud of his career and is confident that Lt. Shea will lead the
Department well. He assured the Committee that he will still be active in the community.
Mark asked what keeps Lt. Shea up at night. She stated that she doesn't know what she doesn't know but stated that Chief
Gaskell has mentored and taught her throughout the last three years. She also emphasized that the mental health and well-

being of her officers are of the utmost importance. She wants to ensure that staff has the right training and tools to do their
job effectively.
Mark thanked Lt. Shea and the Department for the excellent job they do. He wished Chief Gaskell the best and thanked
him for his service. He also wished Lt. Shea good luck in her new role.
Iv.
Update from School
Kerri stated that there was a School Board meeting on Tuesday of the current week.
She stated that health insurance was discussed, and the increase is currently 33%. The School Board had originally
estimated 15% based on the original estimate from SchoolCare. They went out to bid after they found out that
information. Anthem will not work with Pembroke and Health Trust will not be able to provide a quote until April, which
would be for the following year.
She stated that there will be a Special School District on January 20 (Snow date is January 27). They are hoping to adopt
Open Enrollment. There will be a warrant article for Open Enrollment for all grades Kindergarten through 12" grade. She
spoke about enrollment constraints at both Pembroke Hill School and Three Rivers School, which more flexibility for
enrollment at Pembroke Academy. The administrators have provided estimates of how many students they could enroll
without adding more staff. They plan to cap outside enrollment at 25%. This would allow students outside of the district to
apply to attend Pembroke Schools, with the sending town paying a tuition.
In addition, the warrant article will include a provision that no students that are assigned to the Pembroke School District
will be allowed to enroll outside the district unless there are special circumstances that warrant such a decision. This is
currently legal, but this may be changed based on court decisions or legislative actions. There may also be a chance that
Pembroke could be grandfathered in if this is done before it is no longer allowed.
There was discussion about recruiting and marketing of the District at the SAU level. This would be done through a
communications manager position, who will also be responsible for grant activities.
There were questions on how applications would be reviewed in the Open Enrollment process. The concern of
discrimination risks in the application review process was mentioned. Kerri stated that they do have the right to not
accept students that apply, but did echo that discrimination in the process would be prohibited.
Kerri stated that they have met with their legal counsel and had non-public meetings on this topic as well. She also stated
that Concord will be adopting Open Enrollment as well.
Matt asked about the current incentives for students and their families to choose the Pembroke School District. Kerri
mentioned Advanced Placement (AP) Courses, Life/Animal Science, and Concord Regional Technical Center (CRTC).
She also mentioned the possibility of an agriculture program as an example of a program that may provide more appeal.
Gerry voiced concerns on getting residents information about the Open Enrollment article, as well as attendance at the
meeting on January 20th. The School Board has already received approval from the Board of Education, and it will also
need approval from the Superior Court. The Committee and David encouraged Kerri to ensure that the School Board was
prepared and had everything planned appropriately.
Mark emphasized that the explanation to residents be straightforward and easily digestible.
Kerri mentioned that the Board is voting on Monday on the bussing contract. They plan to go with a new company and
highlighted that they will have a spare driver on standby to ensure bus routes are always fulfilled
She stated that the next meeting is on Monday, December 15th at Pembroke Academy. There will also be a Special School
Board Meeting (for the SAU) on January 5'h (Snow Date January 12''). There with be State Representatives in attendance

BUDGET COMMITTEE
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
December 4, 2025
FINAL
Video recordings of Budget Committee meetings can be found at:
https://townhallstreams.com/towns/pembroke_nh
The relative start time of each agenda section is noted below.
Mark LePage, Chairman, called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
I.
Attendance
Budget Committee Present: Mark LePage, Gerry Fleury, Clint Hanson, Brian Seaworth, Matt Miller, Sue Whitbeck,
Kristopher DeLorme, Mariana Beer; Louis Caron
Budget Committee Excused: Jason Mayeu, Gene Gauss
Budget Committee Not Present: None
II. Approval of Minutes - November 13, 2025
Clint Hanson made a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting held on November 13, 2025. Gerry Fleury seconded
the motion.
The motion passed 7-0. Louis Caron abstained.
III.
Town Budget Review - DPW
VJ Ranfos, Public Works Director, was in attendance to present the Public Works Department Budget.
Director Ranfos gave a brief overview of the budget. He spoke about the savings that will be seen from the Electric Trash
Truck, including fuel and container costs. The charger installation has begun with the goal of full operation of the charger
by December 31$. Mariana Beer asked some follow-up questions, including what the plan is for the old vehicle that the
electric truck is replacing. Director Ranfos explained that due to the electric truck being grant funded, the old vehicle must
be put out of commission, including the engine being destroyed.
Director Ranfos continued to review the budget in detail. There were some small savings throughout the Government
Buildings lines with a total decrease of 0.76% 0$995.
The Cemeteries budget lines showed an increase primarily due to mowing services, which increased by $1300 due to a
contractual increase. Matt Miller asked about the monument that was repaired on Buck Street in the amount of $4200 and
David Jodoin, Town Administrator, stated that this came out of the insurance line since it was hit by a truck.
Director Ranfos continued on the Public Works budget lines. He stated that he asked the Selectboard for an additional
employee for eight months of the coming year to help with the workload. The Selectboard compromised on adding this
employee for six months of the year.
He spoke about MS4 (Municipal Separate Storm Water System) requirements, which are overseen by the Environmental
Protection Agency (EPA). There is a street sweeping requirement twice per year now as opposed to once. There was a
three-year contract signed this fall for the sweeping work, which led to an increase in sweeping expenses.
They expect a $2500 decrease in fuel expense due to the new electric trash truck.

He noted that the union contract is still outstanding, and they are unsure of what the final numbers will be for this.
Director Ranfos noted a 6.23% ($17,000) increase in tipping fees due to a price increase from Casella. Conversely, there is
a budgeted decrease of $15,000 (12%) in recycling fees. Gerry inquired about this figure based on historical trends and
current data. Director Ranfos believes that this number can be attained.
He stated that there is an anticipated $14,000 decrease in container fees from having the electric trash truck operational
this upcoming year.
He moved on the Infrastructure Improvements lines. There is a $50,000 increase in Road Repair/Reconstruction to a total
of $850,000. This is due to increased costs for paving. He spoke about the continued maintenance of roads to prevent
larger projects and expenditures.
Director Ranfos spoke about the request for $25,000 for sidewalk repairs. He noted that they have not done sidewalk
repairs in about three or four years. This would be done on parts of Pembroke Street and Pembroke Hill Road. Mariana
asked if this would be put out to bid to a vendor and Director Ranfos confirmed that it would.
David asked Director Ranfos to speak about the infrastructure projects at Memorial Park. Director Ranfos explained that
there are two projects. The first is a drainage projects that has been in progress for approximately four years. The current
clay drainage pipe has failed numerous times. The second project deals with the stabilization of the riverbank that has
been eroding over the years. The total of the two projects will be approximately $1.6 million with $245,000 in loan
forgiveness reimbursed from the State.
Mark asked David to provide an update on health insurance for town employees. The Selectboard has decided to stay with
HealthTrust. David noted that he still needs to do some calculations to get the estimated expense to include in the budget.
Mark asked Director Ranfos what keeps him up at night. The Director stated that it is keeping the same quality and
standard of services, while ensuring that the crew does not get burned out. He added that this was part of the reason why
the seasonal position has been added to the budget. He also stated that he they are currently two down from what they
used to have, and he will continue to push to get back to their previous staffing level.
There was some discussion about the future of recycling in the town. Gerry cautioned that abandoning recycling may not
be the best decision. With local landfills filling up, there may be an increase in the cost of trash disposal due to
transportation fees. He noted that abandoning recycling and the reinstating it may be a costly endeavor.
Mark thanks Director Ranfos and the Public Works Department for their continued work and the great job they do.
IV. Update from School
As Gene Gauss was not in attendance, Mark presented updates from the School District.
He stated that the School Board is discussing a warrant article to go to open enrollment for Pembroke Academy.
There are currently two bids for bussing that are being reviewed.
Healthcare is also still being reviewed.
There was no meeting this week due to weather, but they will meet next week on these topics.
Other Business

The next meeting will be on December 11, 2025, to review the Police Department Budget. On December 18, 2025, the
Sewer and Water Departments will be reviewed
School Budget packets will be available to committee members for review on December 18"*, as well.
Mark is currently collecting numbers to generate the tax sheet.
There was some discussion on the postcard received by residents and David provided an explanation on the assessing
process. Although revaluation happens every five years, measurements and updates are done each year for 25% of the
town each time in between cycles.
VI.
Adjourn
Clint Hanson made a motion to adjourn at 7:33 PM. Sue Whitbeck seconded the motion, and it was approved
unanimously.
Mark LePage, Chairman
For more detailed information, the meetings are now taped and can be seen on www.townhallstreams.com click on
Pembroke NH and look for the day of the meeting under the month.

BUDGET COMMITTEE
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
November 20, 2025
FINAL
Video recordings of Budget Committee meetings can be found at:
https://townhallstreams.com/towns/pembroke_nh
The relative start time of each agenda section is noted below.
Mark LePage, Chairman, called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
I.
Attendance
Budget Committee Present: Mark LePage, Clint Hanson, Brian Seaworth, Matt Miller, Sue Whitbeck, Gene Gauss,
Mariana Beer; Louis Caron
Budget Committee Excused: Jason Mayeu, Gerry Fleury, Kristopher DeLorme
Budget Committee Not Present: None
II. Town Budget Review - Fire, EMS
Chief Paulsen and Assistant Chief Farley were in attendance to present the Fire Department Budget for 2026. The Chief
shared that the overall increase in the Fire Department Budget for the upcoming year is a 3.12% increase.
He explained that the only increase in payroll would be the standard cost of living increase. This includes per diem
personnel. There are also some decreases for training costs this year.
He described the dispatch fees paid to Capital Area Dispatch. This is not a controllable expense and has an increase of
$959 or 1.17% for the year.
He added a slight increase in supplies based on the need for Class A Foam, which is used for brush fires.
Chief Paulsen spoke about equipment that ordered to replace equipment that contains PFAs. There were 23 sets of turnout
gear ordered and put into use this year.
He spoke about the request for a sled that will be used to extricate patients from hazards, whether on land or in water.
They are also seeking a new rescue training mannequin to incorporate into drills and to make drills more realistic.
The largest increase is in the Replacement Equipment Line. Much of this increase is the replacement of the 2.5-inch hose
and a nozzle for the truck and has a cost of $12,201. Hose should be replaced every 20 years, and they would like to get
back on that schedule.
Gene Gauss asked about the Thermal Imaging Batteries at a cost of $1,000 for 2. The Fire Department confirmed that this
is proprietary and brand specific, and this is reflected in the cost.
Mariana Beer asked what NFPA stands for. It stands for the National Fire Protection Association. She also asked about the
Class A Foam and the reasoning for the purchase and asked if Class A Foam expires. Chief Paulsen stated that it does not
expire but also provided a breakdown on how much is need per truck and how much they keep on hand at the station. This
is used typically for brush fires, but also for structures in some cases.
Mark asked about the training mannequin and asked if it would be something that EMS could also use. It cannot be used
interchangeably.

Louis Caron asked about the wage line and if the wages reported for 2025 are year-to-date numbers. This was confirmed.
David Jodoin, Town Administrator, noted that wages are based on call volume. Louis pointed out that wages generally
have been coming in under budget in previous years.
Chief Paulsen gave an overview of some maintenance and repair that has been completed this past year. This upcoming
year, they have a plan for continued maintenance of the fleet and that was also explained.
Mariana asked about the increase in the Computer Maintenance Line. It was explained that this is all software, and an
explanation was given of each piece of software needed for operations.
On behalf of the Committee, Mark expressed appreciation to the Fire Department for their work, including response
times, retention rates and the quality of service.
Brian Seaworth asked about the proposed capital expenditure for a new heavy fire vehicle. With the delivery time being
about two to three years, the Department feels that this is an important piece of equipment to get on the schedule. They
have a 20-year plan for capital expenditures. The Chief also spoke about new technology in these vehicles as well as
keeping their personnel safe. This vehicle was originally purchased in 1999.
Mariana asked if the Department provides opportunities for ride-alongs and they stated that they do and would be happy
to set one up if she was interested.
Chief Paulsen also reviewed the Emergency Management Budget, which saw a total increase of 3.25% (an increase of
$272).
Mark asked about when Emergency Management Procedures would be used. Chief Paulsen stated that it is typically used
for weather events but would also be used for something like an issue in the schools. Assistant Chief Farley added that it
could be used for a hazardous materials situation or any other large emergency event.
Mark asked what keeps the Chief and Assistant Chief up at night. They stated that roadway accidents and distracted
driving are concerning. He also spoke about fire responder behavioral health. Assistant Chief Farley added that it would
be hard to lose a firefighter and need to tell a family member.
Chief Paulsen spoke about replacement equipment and their 8-10-year life span. He spoke about having enough funds
when it is time for another replacement cycle. He added that this is the standard cycle that they have been operating under.
He mentioned preparedness for these purchases forthcoming.
Assistant Chief Farley spoke about concerns with the possible structural updates needed at the Safety Center in the future.
The last renovation was 22 years ago when the Police Department moved in. This could also be impacted as the town
continues to grow. He suggested having a long-term plan for this and urged Budget Committee members to keep this top
of mind.
Mark spoke about a past discussion regarding a possible substation and asked if this would be something that may be
necessary in the future. He asked alternatively if an expansion or renovation of the current Fire Station would be more
beneficial.
Chief Paulsen stated that they would need to look at both options and decide in the future. He noted that the bulk of the
current personnel are located near the current station. Assistant Chief Farley spoke about a report he did on incidents from
2024. Most incidents happened in the Village, up Route 3 and on 106, with some in the in the Route 28 area. He stated
that an in-depth study would need to be completed.
Mark emphasized that he understood that there would need to be a significant need for this to be considered.

There was some discussion as to whether this would be included in the Master Plan. Brian stated that the Master Plan was
completed in 2020 and that it is current. In 5-10 years, it will need revision. He questioned whether this would be through
the Master Plan or through planning activities. He stated that the Budget Committee would be involved as well. He added
that this would most likely be based on growth and that may help the Planning Board assess the cost of the growth to the
people who are driving it.
Mariana asked if there were any immediate concerns in the building. Chief Paulsen spoke about the lack of an exhaust
ventilation system. He spoke about proactive steps they have taken to make it safer but also spoke about the eventual need
for a ventilation system. He also noted the normal wear-and-tear on items within the building.
Chris Gamache, Director of Pembroke EMS, was in attendance to present the 2026 Pembroke EMS Budget.
Director Gamache gave a brief overview of the history of Pembroke EMS. They employ 4 full time, 4 part time and 18 per
diem employees currently. They backup other communities on a regular basis and have approximately 850 to 900 calls per
year with about 450 transports. They currently have two ambulances, but staff one. He spoke about the new ambulance
that was delivered this year (ordered two years ago). They typically have a 6-year useful life (6 years as the primary
vehicle, and 6 years as the backup). There is approximately a three year back order on ambulances currently.
The overall budget is $1,151,156, which represents a 7.62% increase. Most of the increase lies within the payroll lines. He
explained that the ambulance and personnel are fixed costs, and he has trimmed them down as low as possible. He has
planned out all hours for employees for the entirety of next year to come up with these numbers. Health insurance is
showing an increase of 10% and dental insurance is an increase in 5%.
He discussed the uniform costs for the department and the turnover, specifically for per diem employees. The cost is for
new employee uniforms. They also plan to purchase t-shirts for warm weather.
He discussed certifications for paramedics. They have allocated enough money for two of the advanced EMTs for
education. They also subscribe to a service that is an online platform for training. This is available to all staff. The
• They hansaloeaid
Department also does monthly protocol and medication reviews that are uploaded to the platform and required for staff.
Director Gamache spoke about the replacement parts needed for the training mannequin, including veins, skin and trachea
replacement.
He spoke about the Telephone budget line. This includes the station phone, internet and cable. It also provides funds for
the ambulance's cellular technology and Wi-Fi. He spoke about the tablet usage and how it has impacted call times. They
are out of the station in 40 seconds and usually to the scene within 3.5 minutes.
There was an increase in Contracted Billing Services which are provided by Comstar. They have increased their fee from
4% to 5%, which has led to a $5,000 increased from $10,500 per year to a planned $15,500 next year. This is an increase
of approximately 47%. This is based on current call trends.
There was a large increase in Worker's Compensation Insurance of approximately $11,000 (48%). David explained that
this is due to the cost being based on both salaries and claims that may not be specific to EMS.
Director Gamache spoke about the increased costs for supplies. They are keeping less in reserve to combat this. He also
noted that Concord Hospital provides approximately 50% of supplies and some medication at no cost to the department.
He spoke about the Medical Equipment Maintenance and Repair Line. He explained that he uses service agreements to
offset these costs. The cost of repair well exceeds the costs of service agreements.
He talked about the Radio Communications line. He stated that they plan to purchase some pagers and some replacement
radio batteries. He expressed that the Department would like to replace some older radios, but this was removed from this
year's budget to reduce overall costs.

BUDGET COMMITTEE
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
November 13, 2025
FINAL
Video recordings of Budget Committee meetings can be found at:
https://townhallstreams.com/towns/pembroke_nh
The relative start time of each agenda section is noted below.
Mark LePage, Chairman, called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
I.
Attendance
Budget Committee Present: Mark LePage, Gerry Fleury, Clint Hanson, Brian Seaworth, Matt Miller, Sue Whitbeck,
Kristopher DeLorme, Jason Mayeu, Gene Gauss, Mariana Beer
Budget Committee Excused: Louis Caron
Budget Committee Not Present: None
Il.
Approval of Minutes: November 6, 2025
Clint Hanson made a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting held on October 9, 2025. Jason Mayeu seconded the
motion.
The motion passed 10-0.
III.
Town Budget Review - Library, Town Overview
Ryan O'Hora, Pembroke Public Library Director, and Kaitlin Camidge, Chair of Pembroke Public Library Board of
Trustees, were in attendance to present the Library budget.
Ms. Camidge spoke about the Library and how she feels that it is something that Pembroke can be proud of. She spoke
about the three main parts of the Library being the physical building, the resources offered and the staff that runs the
building. She noted that the people portion has been the focus for the past few years due to increasing attendance and the
offerings wanted by the community.
Director O'Hora mentioned a small increase in the operations budget, and a larger increase in the personnel budget. He
expressed that they would like to make the Children's Librarian a full-time benefited position. They have taken a step
approach to this, and the position is currently a 35-hour position with retirement as the only benefit.
Director O'Hora spoke about a phone upgrade being done at the library this past year. They were only able to have one
person on the line at a time previously. This was a safety issue and concern.
He continued to speak about the need for the Children's Librarian position to become full-time. He provided the
Committee with information on total hours and pay for Children's Librarians in the surrounding area for municipalities
with a similar population. Approximately 73% of the libraries polled have a full-time librarian.
Director O'Hora also provided the percentage of the total town budget the Library accounts for. He also provided library
card data and total visits for the past year and previous years since he began tracking.
Gerry Fleury asked about the business internet being a charge of $O. Director O'Hora explained that this used to be its
own bill and is now combined with the phone bill. He added that this has been done for various line items for simplicity of
bookkeeping.

Brian Seaworth inquired about the lines named Electronic Resources and Integrated Library Systems. Director O'Hora
explained that these have been combined into the NH Downloadable Books line. He added that this program is based on
library patron usage.
Gerry asked if there were any significant changes in the HVAC systems in the library that would drive the cost down by
$1,000. Director O'Hora stated that he thinks that this is attainable, and if not, funds would be moved from other lines if
necessary.
Gerry asked about the upgrades that had been completed at the Library and asked Director O'Hora how he felt about
them. Director O'Hora was grateful for the upgrades, which included a new roof and upgraded toilets.
Mariana Beer asked about the increased funding for the Children's Librarian and what the extra time would be used for.
Mr. O'Hora stated that the librarian would be coming in one hour earlier each day and most of this time would be for
planning.
Matt Miller added that this would add stability as well. Mr. O'Hora spoke about ownership and past turnover in the
Children's Librarian position because of the lack of a full-time position.
Ms. Camidge mentioned that Director O'Hora is the only current full-time employee of the Library. She expressed the
importance of having another full-time employee.
Gerry inquired about coverage for vacations and sick time. Director O'Hora explained the difficulties in coverage over the
years for these types of situations. He noted that there used to be issues with only one person staffing the Library by
themselves. Adding a position would be helpful in these situations.
Mark expressed the Board's appreciation to the Director O'Hora and Ms. Camidge for their presentation, and
complimented the Library and their programs.
Sue Whitbeck stated that she attributes the increase in library traffic to Director O'Hora.
David Jodoin, Town Administrator, was in attendance to present and overview of the Town Budget.
He explained that the process has changed this year. The Department Heads presented their recommended budgets to the
Selectboard. David then presented his version of the budget to the Selectboard. He stated that the budget that is in front of
Budget Committee is the Selectboard's version of the budget.
When David went through the budget and cut where he thought was necessary. He explained the summary of the budget
that he compiled for the Committee.
David spoke about specific increases in personnel costs, elections and auditing. He stated that there will be some upgrades
to the town website, which may add some costs since this is still under review.
He mentioned insurance variables that exist. He does not have the finalized selections of employees for their health
insurance plans currently.
Mariana asked about the mowing at cemeteries. David explained that they are in a three-year contract with the mowing
company which includes the cemeteries, Safety Center and Town Hall. He added that this has been found to be more cost
effective and noted the heavy workload of the Department of Public Works. In addition, the employees don't usually take
David spoke about the increase in liability insurance, which is purchased through Primex.

Mark asked about the increase in Unemployment and Worker's Comp Insurance. David explained that Unemployment
Insurance is based on salaries, whereas Worker's Comp Insurance is based on number of accidents, etc. He spoke about a
committee that works on ensuring safety throughout departments that meets quarterly.
David spoke about the Police Department. He spoke about Chief Gaskell retiring. Deputy Chief Shea will take the
position effective January 1, 2026. He spoke about how this may impact salaries, whether there are internal promotions or
outside hires. He commended the department for a quality hiring process.
David explained the increase for Ambulance and the fund balance from the dissolution of Tri-Town being used to offset
the budget.
He spoke about the Fire Department and the possibility of increases since it is currently a volunteer department. It
currently does not operate with any benefits. David has told the Chief that any changes in the future will need to be
discussed with the Budget Committee.
David spoke about hydrant rental fees which are paid to Pembroke Water Works. Due to PFAs issues, Water Works prefers
that this water is only used for actual fires. In accordance with that, the Fire Department is putting a fire hydrant down
near the river for training purposes.
Public Works has a request for a Full-Time Seasonal Employee. David also noted that the Union Contract has not been
finalized for Public Works.
He mentioned the Solid Waste budget costs. There will be some discussions about trash versus recycling and their
respective costs in the future.
David spoke about the Welfare budget. He applauded Muriel for the work that she does with these programs. He iterated
that when people qualify, they legally must receive these benefits. He also spoke about the Community Action Program
and the work that they do in the community.
He mentioned that Parks and Rec budget and commended Rose for the work that she does in this area.
He spoke about a donation received by the Conservation Committee for $70,000. They are looking to purchase a piece of
land for a town forest. There is also a donation of land for 50 acres that is awaiting Selectboard approval.
David added that DPW wanted to bring a bond to the voters this year for Renault, Fairview and Deerpath. He stated that
the State has funds available. He suggested paying off the Main Street bond first. He added that Deerpath would be a
complete reconstruction including drainage work. Fairview also has some drainage issues. This would be between $1.5
and $1.7 million.
There was some discussion on drainage systems and conditions on these roads. Gene inquired about the responsibility of
residents to fix drainage ditches that they have filled in. David gave some history with issues like this from Donna Drive.
Sue asked if there is any documentation when these properties are purchased that states that the drainage cannot be filled
in. David responded that there may be in some instances, but the properties have changed hands many times over the
years.
Brian added some comments on the work that the Roads Committee has been doing. They have been trying to keep up
with the roads as to prevent large projects from having to be done.
Gerry asked if there will be a warrant for the Selectboard to become agents to expend for the Parks and Recreation Capital
Reserve. David stated that there would be one for this, as well as sidewalks.
David spoke about a $35,000 expenditure for a new stage at Memorial Park. He stated that this has support from the CIP
Committee and the Selectboard.

BUDGET COMMITTEE
TOWN OF PEMBROKE, NH
October 9, 2025
FINAL
Video recordings of Budget Committee meetings can be found at:
https://townhallstreams.com/towns/pembroke_nh
The relative start time of each agenda section is noted below.
Mark LePage, Chairman, called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
I.
Attendance
Budget Committee Present: Mark LePage, Gerry Fleury, Clint Hanson, Brian Seaworth, Louis Caron, Matt Miller,
Sue Whitbeck, Kristopher DeLorme, Jason Mayeu, Mariana Beer, Gene Gauss
Budget Committee Excused: None
Budget Committee Not Present: None
II.
Approval of Minutes: April 17, 2025
Gerry Fleury made a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting held on April 17, 2025. Louis Caron seconded the
motion.
The motion passed 9-0.
Matt Miller was not present for the approval of minutes.
III. Election of Officers
Gerry nominated Mark LePage to be the Chair of the Budget Committee. Sue Whitbeck seconded the motion. Clint
Hanson moved that nominations be closed.
The motion passed 9-0.
Mark nominated Gerry to be the Vice Chair of the Budget Committee. Gene Gauss seconded the motion.
The motion passed 9-0.
Matt was not present for the votes, but was in attendance directly after the votes were completed.
IV.
Updates from School & Town on Current Status and What's Coming
Mark asked Gene to provide an update on the SchoolCare situation, which deals with the healthcare offered to school
staff. The School Board received notice from SchoolCare that there was a $30 million shortfall for the company.
Pembroke's portion of that is approximately $630,000. There is approximately $430,000 in remaining funds that the
School Board has voted to put towards the SchoolCare balance. This would have been returned to the taxpayers as tax
relief if this had not occurred.
The School Board has elected to wait to pay the balance until December of 2025 to allow legal review and to gather more
information. The School Board is trying to determine how and when they will pay the balance. Current options include
covering some special ed costs out of the Special Education Trust to free up general funds to apply to the shortfall. The
use of any potential surplus at the end of the year to cover costs is also a possibility.

The School Board has also requested that a representative from SchoolCare attend a School Board Meeting to provide
more information.
Gene mentioned that SchoolCare had been coming in with a much lower year over year increase on their bid than other
providers in recent years. Before any funds are released, there will be a review of the entirety of the situation.
Gene also notified the Committee that 12 students have gone to Prospect Mountain School from Epsom (10) and
Chichester (2). This is approximately $200,000 in revenue that the SAU is not currently receiving from the respective
towns. This is a violation of the Administrative and Resource Education Agreement (AREA agreement as Pembroke
Academy is not an open enrollment school. There is a case in the Supreme Court with the Town of Pittsfield for a similar
matter and the School Board is awaiting a decision on this to determine how to proceed.
There is also a deficit of $282,882 in expected State Adequate Education Aid funding. Gene provided a breakdown of this
number for the Committee.
Gene noted that there is more information forthcoming on all the information provided at this meeting.
Mark stated that Jess Bickford, Superintendent of Schools, had reached out to both Mark and Gerry to offer a meeting
regarding the SchoolCare situation.
Gerry spoke about his concern with pulling funds from the Special Education Capital Reserve to cover the outstanding
SchoolCare balance. He did some research on the applicable uses of the Special Education Capital Reserve and as a
Trustee of Trust Funds, he could not vote for such a use of funds unless he had sign off from the State Attorney General.
Gene emphasized that there would be more review including a legal review of this possibility. He also stated that there is a
possibility that there may be a surplus at the end of the school year that may cover the approximately $200,000 remaining.
Gerry spoke about the possibility of encumbering funds and how that would look from an accounting standpoint. Gene
stated that the MS-25 could possibly be amended to allow for the encumbrance.
Gerry requested the actuary information for his review from SchoolCare and Gene agreed to facilitate that process.
Brian Seaworth stated that the average daily attendance determines the State Adequacy Aid funding. He would like to
know if Pembroke is facing a drop in enrollment. Gene stated that this is primarily due to school choice and a smaller
number of moves-aways. He stated that Prospect Mountain School is offering 80% tuition for students based on the school
that they are supposed to attend. The towns are picking up the bill for this, and some are not towns aware.
Brian added that last year, Patty Sherman had stated last year that there were many reasons for the enrollment decreases.
Mark noted that the effects of Education Freedom Accounts (EFAs) have yet to be seen.
Matt mentioned the 80% tuition offering from Prospect Mountain School. He wanted clarification on who Prospect
Mountain School is trying to collect tuition from. Gene stated that they were trying to collect from Epsom and Chichester.
Mark clarified that this is a tactic to try and draw in students. There was discussion on Prospect Mountain School and their
recruiting practices.
Clint spoke about the implications of the AREA Agreement being violated
Gene stated that Epsom and Chichester
are currently encumbering funds until they determine what entity should receive
those funds. Pembroke will not be receiving any funds until this determination is made.
Gene mentioned the Jess Bickford is doing a great job and is very effective and prepared. She is accessible to School
Board members and is walking through schools weekly. Her presence is known.
Gerry and Mark met with Jess Bickford in August. She was extremely willing to have a meeting and is looking forward to

meeting again. Mark emphasized that he was impressed by her proactive approach.
Gerry spoke about the audit report being issued for 2023. Most material weaknesses have been resolved. It was also filed
on time. There is one observation remaining, which states that there are multiple people who have access to the bank
account. David Jodoin explained that sometimes multiple people need to have access and detailed the Town's system for
their banking.
Gerry stated that the auditors thought that there should be a view only option for some users. Gene noted that this has
since been explained to the auditors and they have signed off on the current process. The office is now fully staffed and
the lack of segregation of duties has been resolved to some degree.
Mark stated that they would now discuss Town updates.
David explained that they are in contract negotiations with Public Works for their Collective Bargaining Agreement
(CBA).
The Selectboard and David are reviewing different insurance providers currently and are now in detailed discussions with
ne provider and exploring offerings. Three providers were contacted in total. The Town also pulled out from the Suncoo
Talley Regional Towns. They will pursue individual insurance for the Town. The Selectboard will be having
presentation on this matter from the insurance provider that they are currently working with.
This year the budget process with the Selectmen is changing. Normally David would sit with the Department Heads and
then craft a budget to give to the Selectmen. This year the Department Heads are meeting with the Selectmen to review
their budget proposals. When they are done, David will be giving the Selectmen his budget recommendations. The
selectmen will then review and deliberate what they will present to the Budget Committee
Matt added that healthcare inflation is out of control. He explained the HealthTrust has shown double digit increases year
over year for some time.
He also spoke about necessary gear like radios, firearms etc. outpacing inflation consistently.
Lastly, he explained that there have not been discussions on revenues up until this point, but those discussions will be
taking place.
David stated that the culvert replacement and stabilization of the bank at Memorial Park have been approved.
Matt and David discussed budget review and expenditures that may occur before the budgets are finalized. This included a
discussion on encumbrances and how they show as expenditures.
Gerry gave a summary of trash costs. September starts a new year on the trash contract. In August, the trash rate was
$110.94 per ton. In September, this number increased to $117.93 per ton. The trash rate has increased $6.99 per ton year
over year. This is contractual and will remain the same rate through next August. Recycling is a floating rate and
fluctuates throughout the year. The rate for August was $134.29 and has increased to $141.54, an increase of $7.15 per
ton.
Out of concern for this, the Solid Waste Committee toured the Casella Facility in Charlestown, Massachusetts. He
believes that the rate continues to rise because Casella has no reason to control costs because Massachusetts mandates
recycling. He spoke about the overall process at the plant.
He continued that both Hooksett and Allenstown have abandoned recycling. He suggested that Pembroke proceeds with
caution. There are some concerns with that availability of landfills, which may drive costs up. If trash cannot be buried
here, it will need to be transported to another state. This will increase costs significantly.
